extension.description: Official repository for the Starfleet Kodi addon.

extension.summary: Starfleet - TV, Movies, Live TV, Sports, Radio, Adult
extension.description: All-in-one Kodi plugin. TV, Movies, Live TV, Sports, Free Streaming, Adult (PIN-protected), Radio. Torrent/debrid sources via Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox. Elementum support for magnet playback.
extension.news:
v2.3.655 - Telegram linking fixed: the QR code on screen could be an old one (Kodi kept showing the first picture after the code was renewed) and the screen did not close even when Telegram showed the account as linked. Each renewed code now gets its own picture, a scan is noticed within a few seconds, and a sign-in that Telegram finished is recognised however the wait ended. A link attempt that was cancelled or timed out no longer counts as "linked" (Settings said so and the Telegram sources came back empty); it counts only once Telegram has really signed the account in. Anticipated movies / shows: the hero's "More Info" now opens the full detail screen (it opened a plain text box with no cast), and that screen has a new "Cast / More Films" button - Right of Add to Favorites - that lists the whole cast; pick an actor to see what else they are in. v2.3.654 - Lighter pre-loading: the next episode (and a new episode on its air day) is prepared with the torrent / debrid search only - no free sites, embed players, personal library, Easynews or Requests - and only with the sources that are switched on; choosing a title yourself still does the full search. New: your SIMKL / Trakt My List is kept up to date in the background - one quick "has anything changed?" check when Kodi starts, when Home opens and every 15 minutes, and the lists (movies, shows, anime) and watched ticks are fetched again only when the account changed, then kept on disk, so a section opens at once and matches the account even on a Fire TV Stick. New option (Settings > Adult Section, off by default): get the Adult widgets ready in the background after Kodi starts and hourly. v2.3.653 - SIMKL progress fixes: shows that SIMKL lists as being watched but gives no "next episode" for (any show you began after its first episode - a later season of a long show, a season 2 started without season 1) were left out of Continue Watching; they are back, continuing after the last episode watched. Episodes and films marked watched on your SIMKL account (another device, another app, before this add-on kept a history) now show as watched here. A watched mark that could not be sent to SIMKL (no connection, SIMKL busy) is kept and sent later instead of being lost. Marking an episode, a season or a film watched (or unwatched) by hand now also goes to your SIMKL and Trakt accounts (it used to stay on this device), and with only Trakt paired the watched ticks come from Trakt too, so a second device shows the same ticks. v2.3.652 - New: Smart Search (Movies and TV Shows menus) - say what you want, "a 90 minute thriller like Prisoners but lighter", "comedy series with short episodes from the 90s", "best sci-fi with Tom Hanks" - and TMDB answers it; Coming up (same menus) - one calendar of your shows' next episodes, followed teams' games, anime airing and the movies about to open. New episodes of the shows you watch are searched for on the day they air and get a notice ("Watch now?") when their links appear; the next episode of what you are watching is now prepared even with auto-play-next off. Faster: the source list opens 2 s after the best sources are in instead of waiting for the slow free sites and your Requests library (15 s down to 2-5 s for a typical show; setting: Open the source list as soon as the best sources are in). v2.3.651 - Faster source lists: the picker for a movie, show or anime episode opens in about 2 s instead of 4-8 s (the best three torrent sources first, release-site rows no longer held back, see Settings > Torrent Sources > Torrent sources). More releases: 4K releases with a foreign-language title in front and DVD rips are listed again. New: HDR / Dolby Vision / Atmos / REMUX tags on the sources, upscaled "4K" releases and (if you say your TV has no Dolby Vision) Dolby Vision-only releases are listed last; sources that keep finding nothing are switched off for a day, shown in "Why isn't this working?", with a button to switch them back on. v2.3.650 - A much smaller add-on: 25 MB down to about 9 MB. The sports icons are stored at the size they are shown, compiled Python caches and a stray cache file no longer ship, and the copies of the Cloudflare helper (two of them, used only by the scrapers) moved into the Starfleet Scrapers module. Nothing looks or behaves differently. v2.3.649 - Home: the Profile button now shows recommendations picked for the active profile - Recommended Movies, Recommended Shows and "Because you watched ..." rows - built from what that profile watches (its own history plus the linked SIMKL or Trakt, favouring recent and well-rated titles) using TMDB's "people who liked this also watched" lists; a Kids profile gets kid-safe picks, and a profile with no history yet sees trending and top-rated rows. Fixed: the Anticipated Movies / Shows rows now play their trailers when highlighted, like the other rows. v2.3.648 - Profiles: each person keeps their own progress, Continue Watching, favourites, My Teams and their own SIMKL / Trakt / WeTrakr accounts, and you switch with the Profile button at the top right of Home - no logging in or out. The selector lists the profiles by name and can create one; Settings > Profiles manages them. A profile can be Adult or Kids, hide the Adult section, limit what it shows to little kids / 7+ / 14+, and have its own PIN; an optional Parent PIN keeps a Kids profile out of Settings and profile changes. Your existing history is the first profile ("Main"), nothing is lost. Tonight now shows only what belongs to the section you open it from (games under Sports, episodes under TV Shows, new anime under Anime). Sports streams show their quality (1080p / 720p / SD). v2.3.647 - New: My Teams (follow teams from any game list or Sports > My Teams: they lead the Sports tab on Home with live scores and start times, and Starfleet can alert you when their game goes live, goes to overtime or gets close; hold OK on a game to follow); Tonight (TV Shows or Sports: your teams' games, your shows' next episodes and anime episodes airing, in local time); Just Play (Settings > General: skip the source list - the best source plays, and if it does not play the next one starts by itself, for movies, TV and sports, and Starfleet learns which sources work for you); the next episode now starts instantly (it is searched while you watch, Settings > TV Shows); "Why isn't this working?" in Settings > General checks your setup and tells you what to fix. Also: Settings: pairing status and unpairing are now two separate buttons for Trakt, SIMKL, WeTrakr and TMDB. "Check ... pairing status" only reports (for Trakt and SIMKL it also asks the service whether the pairing still works, and shows the account name); "Unpair ..." asks for confirmation and then forgets the pairing. v2.3.646 - TV Shows and Movies: a section for each watch-tracking account you have paired, named after it (Simkl, Trakt, WeTrakr), right after Favorites. The TV Shows selector lists the shows on that account with how far through each one you are, and the Movies selector lists its movies; the details shown (overview, genres, rating, runtime, network, posters) come from the account's own service where it provides them (Simkl fully, Trakt for text; WeTrakr has no read access, so its section lists what Starfleet has sent it). Anything the service does not provide - a poster, a backdrop, an overview, or all of it - comes from TMDB instead. The Anime selector gets the same sections for Simkl (its anime list, series and films) and Trakt (its anime-tagged shows and films). v2.3.645 - Adult: the New Releases and Recently Added rows on Home now show only films that have a release on XXXClub, which keeps Home quick to load (each answer is remembered, so refreshes cost nothing). Opening New Releases or Recently Added itself still lists every film that has any source. Sports: every game row now starts with its start time in your own time zone (Today 8:00 PM), live games show the clock and score (LIVE 7:25 - 1st Celtics 10 - 9 Knicks), finished games are no longer listed, and games that showed TBD have their times back. v2.3.644 - New Anime section (a tab on Home and an entry in the main menu): Trending, Popular This Season, Airing Now, Upcoming Next Season, Top Rated, Anime Movies, New Anime Movies, Browse by Genre and Search, listed from AniList and opened through the normal show / season / episode pages so favourites, watched marks and the source picker work as usual. Starting Starfleet is lighter: the Live TV and Radio channel lists on Home load when you open that tab, and the TV guide (including the Plex, LG and Pluto guides, now taken from the services themselves) is built only when you launch it. Settings: switch Elementum off (torrents then need a debrid service), hide releases dubbed in Russian / Ukrainian or in every other language, and the existing source options are unchanged. Season and episode lists open much faster. Samsung TV+ and Roku Channel are removed from Live TV (neither offers a public channel list). v2.3.643 - Release sites as a Movies/TV source: RapidMoviez, ReleaseBB, Scene-RLS and MyVideoLinks hoster links appear as [DDL] rows when your debrid service covers the host (Settings > Torrent Sources to switch them off). Adult gains WhoresHub and PornRewind. v2.3.642 - Much faster Movie and TV source search (about 1.3 s instead of 5.5 s) with more results: slow low-yield sources (Snowfl, FileMood, Bitsearch) are now off by default, and the recommended preset matches. v2.3.641 - Settings > Torrent Sources > Scraper module: pick Starfleet Scrapers only, Starfleet plus the other scraper modules installed on the device, or those modules only, and choose which of them to use. New in Live TV: CDN Live sports and TV channels by country; Sports gains CDN Live and match-feed streams. v2.3.640 - New: Settings > Torrent Sources lets you set the highest resolution to look for and the lowest to keep (an older TV has no use for 4K releases), TimStreams 24/7 channels in Live TV, TimStreams events work again, adult scenes gain eight sites and the 107 tube sites are back with xHamster fixed. Scraping moved into its own add-on, Starfleet Scrapers (installed automatically): adult, movie and TV hosters, torrent / usenet search for debrid, sports, live TV and radio scrapers now update separately, so a broken site can be fixed without a full Starfleet update. Menus, metadata, widgets, favourites and debrid pairing stay in Starfleet exactly as they were. New: Starfleet can also run other installed scraper modules and merge their results with its own (Settings > Torrent Sources), torrent API sources return their full lists instead of the first 40, and Starfleet Scrapers can be chosen as the scraper module of other add-ons that load one. WeTrakr updated to match WeTrakr's current Kodi client: a saved pairing that WeTrakr no longer accepts is detected (instead of silently sending nothing) and you are asked to pair again, the Now Playing session is refreshed about every 30 seconds while you watch, the pairing page uses the current activation address, and you can turn on an optional 1-10 rating prompt after finishing a movie or episode. v2.3.639 - Torrent sources no longer die with one server: Comet, Zilean and StremThru now fall back to additional public instances when the first is down or busy, and YTS has a new mirror and skips dead domains instead of returning nothing. v2.3.638 - Live TV and links that use DASH (.mpd) manifests now play: the player is set up with inputstream.adaptive for live and on-demand DASH, with ClearKey and Widevine licence details when the stream needs them. This opens the roughly 230 DASH channels in the IPTV-org lists. v2.3.637 - New in Live TV: Roku Channel (259 channels), LG Channels (US, about 130 working channels; the ones LG refuses are hidden) and IPTV-org Live TV by Country - the newest public iptv-org lists for 189 countries sorted by country and category, with the over-the-air networks and local stations of the USA and Canada (ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX, PBS, CBC, CTV and more) in their own group at the top. Roku and LG channels carry their own program guide; IPTV-org channels of the countries you pick (default US and Canada, change it from the IPTV-org menu) are matched to a current guide when you use Export to TV Guide. v2.3.636 - Requires Starfleet Resolver 1.3.0, which resolves more live sports pages (game pages that embed a known player now resolve end to end, direct playlists pass through, new embed formats and the gsports.lat player). Updating this add-on updates the resolver in the same step. v2.3.635 - Now requires Starfleet Resolver 1.2.0 or newer, so updating the plugin also installs or updates the resolver in the same step (Kodi pulls it in as a required add-on). The resolver 1.2.0 adds Mega-Debrid pairing (login and password, or imported from this add-on's Mega-Debrid settings), uses TorBox for sites no host list names, and gains the Program add-on 'Starfleet Resolver' (Add-ons > Program add-ons) for pairing debrid accounts and testing links. v2.3.634 - The Starfleet Resolver now carries its own copy of every ResolveURL host resolver (296 resolvers, 1296 domains, adult hosts included), so hosts are resolved by Starfleet first and the installed ResolveURL is only the last-chance fallback. It is faster: secure connections are set up once per session instead of for every request, and our own resolvers (Voe, StreamTape, MixDrop, DoodStream and its clones, the sports players) answer in about a second or less. New or fixed hosts: Eporner, Pornhub, XHamster and the new file-code player clones (ubgaiwa, sgoabjgio, igbsa and future ones); dead hosts such as GoUnlimited now fail at once with a clean message. Debrid accounts: the resolver imports the keys typed in this add-on and any paired in ResolveURL (checked before they are kept), has its own Settings page to pair Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox, Debrid-Link and Offcloud, and Debrid-Link and Offcloud can now fetch a torrent that is not cached yet. Samsung TV Plus and Plex channels were re-tested and play. v2.3.633 - Starfleet Resolver, more debrid services, and a wrong-episodes fix. (1) NEW add-on Starfleet Resolver (installed automatically) resolves video hosts faster than before: it handles Voe (ResolveURL fails every current Voe link; this one opens them in about a second), DoodStream and its clone domains, StreamTape, MixDrop, the sports players (embed.st, embedsports, streame.center, rockylive, DLHD and more) and free file hosts such as MediaFire, Gofile, Pixeldrain, Dropbox, Google Drive and Sendspace. ResolveURL stays installed as the fallback (limited to 14 seconds) and your debrid accounts are used for file lockers that need them. (2) Debrid pairing now covers Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox, Debrid-Link and Offcloud from Settings (new Debrid-Link and Offcloud sections, with the on-screen code and QR). Torrents and hoster links go through every paired service. (3) FIX: a season could list episodes from a different show with the same name (Dark Matter season 2 showed episodes 11 to 13 of the 2015 series). Extra episodes from the cross-check sources are now only accepted from the show with the same start year and never from before the show began. v2.3.632 - Fresh tracker list for torrents, and one more torrent source. Magnets now get the community-maintained list of working public trackers (the 'best' list from the ngosang trackerslist project, refreshed daily and kept in the addon folder; if it cannot be downloaded the last copy or a built-in list is used). It is added to every magnet the addon builds from a bare info-hash, to magnets sent to your debrid service (more ways for a service to fetch a torrent it does not have cached), and to magnets handed to Elementum. A magnet that already carries six or more trackers is left alone. NEW source: TorrentKitty (a DHT index; every result is a real info-hash, but it has no seed counts, so results sort after the others). It is off by default: turn it on under Settings, torrent sources. Looked at but not added: UIndex and Idope (Cloudflare check), Solid Torrents (server error), BTSOW (not reachable); TorrentsCSV, Knaben, Pirate Bay, LimeTorrents, Nyaa and Bitsearch were already covered. v2.3.631 - Monday Night Football fixes (Bills at Rams). (1) StreamEast, BuffStreams and SportSurge pointed at a shared player whose playlist answered but whose video segments all returned 404 (the NFL feed behind it was not delivering). Links from the game-page sites are now only listed when a real video segment can be fetched. (2) TopStreamer, which was live for this game (a fresh feed, segments downloaded as real video, ads stripped), was left out because the list was capped at 12 links and it came last; it is now tried early and the cap is 16. (3) Pre-resolved NFL links and the NFL24 feed were listed while dead (the playlist gave 403, or the server did not answer for 40 seconds); both are now dropped when no segment list comes back. NFL Network works through MethStreams, TimStreams, Streamed, PlayoffsStream and 720pStream. RedZone had no working source tonight (it is a Sunday channel). v2.3.630 - Fixes from your desktop log. (1) PlayoffsStream and 720pStream opened and then closed at once: their playlist address ends in .ts, so the player treated it as raw video (log: ffmpegdirect, mpegts, eof). It is now served as HLS through the local relay (tested: master playlist, 720p playlist, decryption key and video segments all fetched through it). (2) SlapStreams gave HTTP 403: its playlist addresses stop working about two minutes after they are made, and the list was kept for five minutes. SlapStreams is now looked up again at the moment you pick it, and the stream list is kept for 90 seconds instead of five minutes. LINK 3 (streame.center) now resolves to a playlist; LINK 4 (rockylive) is resolved too but its feed was not up for this game. (3) OnHockey listed 20 to 35 links per game and about half never played. Each one is now checked side by side: playlists must list segments, player pages must resolve to a playlist, duplicates are listed once, and hosts that never worked are skipped (about 21 of 34 links are kept for Senators-Devils). (4) Free feeds from the 24all sites are capped by the site at 360p (one 640x360 version at 476 kbps); their higher quality is premium only (the site answers 'Premium Access Token Not Provided'), so use PlayoffsStream or 720pStream, iHDStreams or StreamEast for a 720p picture. DLHD (dlive.sx) returned nothing: its servers are not answering. v2.3.629 - Faster stream search for every sport. ROOT CAUSE of the slow, incomplete lists: every new HTTPS connection reloaded the whole certificate bundle (0.3 to 1 second of CPU each), and a stream search opens dozens of connections at once. The addon now shares one certificate context between connections, loaded once; certificates and host names are still fully checked (tested: expired, wrong-host and self-signed sites are still refused). Measured here: 20 parallel requests 0.6 s with the bundle loaded once instead of 4 times that or more, and a whole NHL stream search 9.6 s instead of 16 s. Also: sources whose sites are down (Hoofoot, the old StreamEast address, the old TimStreams list) are parked for 30 minutes after the first failure instead of being retried on every game, and the mirror-crawling sources now start 2 seconds after the built-in live sites instead of 4 to 5. NBA test on the Thunder-Hawks game: 17 streams from 8 sources (BuffStreams, 720pStream, PlayoffsStream, RoxieStreams, StreamEast, iHDStreams, NBA24ALL, SportSurge). v2.3.628 - Live sites were being starved on the desktop: VoloKit, RoxieStreams, GStream24, Streamed and Sportzone did not show in your MLB search while others did. Cause found by profiling: every new HTTPS connection reloads the certificate bundle (about 0.3 to 1 second of CPU each), and the mirror-crawling sources (SportSurge made 73 connections, TVNow, FalconStreams, BuffStreams) used all of it in the first seconds, so the live sites only finished 2 or 3 of their 12 links before the cut-off. Now: the live sites run first and the crawlers start 4 to 5 seconds later; the sources most likely to work are tried first; the cut-off is 12 seconds instead of 8 and the early exit waits for 5 results (was 3). Same game on my PC: 7 streams in the list (MLB24, MethStreams, VoloKit, GStream24, Streamed, RoxieStreams) instead of 4. v2.3.627 - Live sites fixed during the MLB game (Dodgers-Brewers). Three game-page sites listed the game but gave no stream: StreamEast, BuffStreams and SportSurge all use a shared player whose playlist address is hidden as base64 and has no .m3u8 in its name; the addon now follows it and checks that it really answers with a playlist. iHDStreams keeps its player address in a short encoded block and double-XORs it (the two passes cancel out), so it now resolves too; addresses written with JSON escape codes are cleaned. When two sites embed the same player it is listed once. Verified live: a full search for the live game now returns 8 playable streams (GStream24, VoloKit, RoxieStreams, MethStreams, Streamed, StreamEast, Sportzone, iHDStreams), each playlist and a video segment fetched. Still not working for this game: StreamEast VG (page name differs), StreamCenter and Streamsify (their game pages are gone once a game starts) and RockyLive's own feed (its embed is not live). v2.3.626 - Live MLB fixes found while testing the Dodgers-Brewers game. (1) The free live feed on the MLB24/NHL24/NFL24/NBA24 sites was missed while a game showed the site's 'W' (on air) status; the addon picked the finished game before it and offered only its replay. 'W' now counts as live. (2) The built-in live sites (Streamed, VoloKit, GStream24, RoxieStreams, MethStreams, Sportzone...) were being starved on a busy search: BuffStreams tried up to 80 mirrors and FalconStreams up to 60, mostly dead hosts, so those sources timed out with nothing. BuffStreams now tries at most 24 mirrors and FalconStreams 18, the live sites get their own thread and a longer allowance, and the game pages are looked up in parallel with the schedule lists. Result on the live game: 6 working streams (MLB24, VoloKit, Streamed, BuffStreams x2, MethStreams) instead of 1. v2.3.625 - Live sports: wrong-game streams and the FalconStreams link that would not play. Your log showed two causes. (1) FalconStreams (and other sources) handed over an embed.st page address that Kodi cannot open ('error probing input format'); every embed.st / embedsports.me link is now turned into the real playlist, and dropped when the game is not live. (2) BuffStreams mirrors (SoccerStreams, Apexstreams) and similar sites give out a numbered channel that shows whatever is on that channel right now, so before a game those played a different event. Those channel-based sources (BuffStreams mirrors, RoxieStreams, StreamCenter and the other schedule sites) are now only offered from 45 minutes before the start time, which the event list now passes along. Also fixed: page addresses written without a host ('https:///premiumtv/...') are repaired, and TopStreamer NBA pages (a direct playlist with a session id) are handled. Games tip off in the evening: if a source still plays the wrong game once the game is on, tell me the source name and game. v2.3.624 - Live sports: PlayoffsStream and 720pStream now play, TopStreamer added, and free game replays from the 24all sites. PlayoffsStream and 720pStream use embedsports.me players; the addon now follows that player's own sign-in steps and gets a 720p/480p playlist (checked live on the NHL Network feed: playlist, key and video segments all fetched). OnHockey links to the same player are no longer hidden. TopStreamer (NFL and NBA schedule pages): the site publishes its live playlist over a websocket instead of a file, so the addon reads it through its local relay on every playlist refresh, drops ad breaks and offers the qualities it lists. Tested with a simulated live feed; each channel is only offered while the site's own feed is live, so it will show up at game time (the real feed is untested until then). REPLAYS: Replay > NHL, MLB, NFL and NBA games now also list the free full-game replay from nhl24all, mlb24all, nfl24all and nba24all when one exists (only the latest few finished games have one; NHL and MLB were checked, 170 to 240 minute playlists). Please test during a live game and send the Kodi log if a source is missing. v2.3.623 - Live sports: RoxieStreams and MethStreams added. RoxieStreams (NHL, NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, fighting, motorsports) gives a direct live playlist; checked live: Sabres-Panthers and NFL both return a playlist. MethStreams (NHL, NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, MMA, boxing, college football, WWE, F1) lists each game with several players; the ones the addon can decode are used first. StreamCenter, StreamEast, FSportsHD and GStream24 were already added in 2.3.622. v2.3.622 - Live sports: more built-in sources and more sports. NEW sources, each looked up only when you open a game: StreamCenter (hockey, football, basketball, baseball, soccer), StreamHD (soccer and world sports), Streamsify, SportSurge (new address), RockyLive (NHL, NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, UFC, boxing and more; its players are embed.st feeds the addon already decodes) and TimStreams (24/7 sports channels, with its anti-bot check now solved by the addon itself). Player pages are now followed up to five steps (page, iframe, encoded address, number-array address, server-side decryption) instead of one, and malformed iframe addresses are repaired. Formula 1 and MotoGP pages were added to the providers that carry them (StreamEast, GStream24, VoloKit, FSportsHD, iHDStreams, BuffStreams). Checked live: RockyLive and VoloKit links resolve to embed.st playlists, TimStreams NHL Network gives a live playlist, StreamHD gives a live playlist. StreamCenter, Streamsify and SportSurge only publish their players once a game is on, so their links show up around game time. Please test during a live game and send the Kodi log if a source is missing. v2.3.621 - Live sports: embed.st streams now play, plus Streamed and nine more schedule sites. embed.st and the embedsports sites (the players behind DaddyLive events, OnHockey links and Streamed) answer with an encrypted playlist address; the addon now decodes it itself (no extra library needed) and plays the stream. Checked live on the NHL Network feed: a real HLS playlist with segments. NEW sources, each looked up only when you open a game (so lists stay fast): Streamed (streamed.pk, all sports incl. NHL Network and ESPN-style 24/7 feeds), StreamEast (streameast.cool and the .vg mirror), PlayoffsStream, 720pStream, iHDStreams, FSportsHD, GStream24, VoloKit and BuffStreams (mybuffstreams.plus). Those pages only carry a player once a game is on or about to start, so their links appear around game time; the NHL Network and the Sabres-Panthers lookups were tested live, the rest are tested up to the schedule listing. Still not playable: embedsports.me players (used by PlayoffsStream and 720pStream) and TimStreams (its anti-bot check). Also: the old StreamEast address (streameasti.is) and Hoofoot are down and the old SportSurge address is behind a Cloudflare check; those entries fail quickly and the new sources cover the same games. v2.3.620 - Torrent and debrid sources checked one by one (65 search functions, all four test titles, AllDebrid and Premiumize accounts valid, cached links play). FIXED: Debrid Media Manager (DMM) was answering 403 because it now issues its own security token; the addon asks for it first (40 results again). Torrent9 moved to a new address. EXT.to and BT4G were returning nothing because their Cloudflare pass had expired; both were refreshed and republished. Still down on this network: MagnetDL, GloDLS, TorrentProject2, Torrentz2, AnimeTosho feed, Demonoid and XXXTor (their servers refuse the connection), TorLock and YourBitTorrent (Cloudflare block pages), Bittorrented (invite only) and ApacheTorrents (redesigned, search no longer returns the title). Working: Torrentio, Comet, MediaFusion, Meteor, StremThru, Zilean, Bitmagnet, AIOStreams, TorrentsDB, Peerflix, DMM, YTS, EZTV, TPB, 1337x, Knaben, KickAss, LimeTorrents, TorrentDownloads, TorrentFunk, TorrentGalaxy, Snowfl, RARBG dump, Rutor and more. v2.3.619 - Replays: new sources, NFL fixed, adaptive quality. UFC and Boxing now also use mmareplays.com (one page per fight, plus the full-card sources from fullfightreplays.com); an event that two sites list under different names is now one entry (for example 'UFC Vegas 122' and 'UFC Fight Night 290: Allen vs. Duncan'). NFL Replay was showing junk links: nfl-video.com now points its buttons at unrelated TV-schedule pages that hold the real player, so those pages are opened and the Dailymotion or OK.ru video inside is used (about 2 of 3 buttons carry a playable embed). ADAPTIVE QUALITY: OK.ru (five sizes from 144p to 720p) and Dailymotion are now played as adaptive HLS, so the player switches quality on its own as your connection changes. If HLS is off or unavailable the file size is picked from a quick speed test instead. New settings (General): Replay quality limit (Auto, up to 1080p, 720p, 480p or 360p) and Replays: adaptive streaming on/off. Note: Dailymotion copies of UFC cards only go up to 480p and playmate.to offers a single 1080p stream, so OK.ru is the only source with a real 720p ladder. v2.3.618 - NHL Replay rebuilt: one entry per game, grouped by date, with a source picker. Sports > Replay > NHL now lists every date (about 70 so far, back to last season's playoffs) and the games on it as 'Away @ Home' with no score. Opening a game offers: Full Game (hockeyreplays.com, OK.ru), Recap - Long (about 10 min condensed game from nhlrecaps.net), Recap - Short (about 5 min recap from nhlrecaps.net) and a spoiler-free highlights video from dtmts.com (last few days). The recaps play as plain MP4 files, which avoids the NHL.com stream format Kodi could not play before. Games that have these links skip the slow torrent search, so the picker opens in about 3 seconds; older torrent sources are still listed when a game has no direct link. v2.3.617 - Adult sources checked one by one (179 Scenes and Movies sites: listing, categories, search, stream) and the broken ones fixed. NEW: PornHills in Scenes (Latest, 76 categories with paging, search, direct MP4). XMovix and PelisXPorno were already in Movies; both were re-checked and work, PelisXPorno now has its own category browser and correct titles, and XMovix titles no longer show raw codes. v2.3.550 - Real title-filter bug found from a fresh kodi.log: searching "L.A.'s Finest S01E01" found 143 real raw candidates across 9 different torrent sources (Torrentio/Knaben/EZTV/TorrentFunk/Tordl/Torrentz2/LimeTorrents/FileMood/EXTto), and every single one got rejected by the shared title-match filter, ending in "0 torrents found" even though The Pirate Bay's own site plainly has this exact show (confirmed live via a direct link). Root cause: the filter splits a query into words on any non-word character, so "L.A.'s Finest" became the four tokens l/a/s/finest - but it then drops every single-character token before building the actual search phrase, leaving just "finest" - and the check that the query must start the candidate's title required everything before that match to be a real dictionary skip-word (a/an/the/etc), which "l"/"a"/"s" obviously aren't, so a real candidate like "L.A.'s.Finest.S01E01..." got rejected purely for containing the exact abbreviation the query itself had already given up on matching. Found a second, compounding bug alongside it: the candidate-side text normalization stripped curly smart quotes but never the plain straight apostrophe real torrent filenames actually use, so "LA's Finest" left "la's" glued into one 4-character token instead of splitting into "la"/"s" the way the fix above expected. Fixed both, plus extended the same short-leftover-word tolerance to the middle of a multi-word phrase, not just the very start - confirmed live this was the same root issue behind titles like "Ocean's Eleven" or "Grey's Anatomy" only matching correctly when the apostrophe happens to fall at the very end. Verified against a full regression suite including the original "FROM"/"Farmhouse Rules" and "Found"/"Virgin River" false-positive bugs this filter already existed to prevent - all still correctly rejected, plus a deliberately unrelated random-word candidate still correctly rejected. This one shared filter function backs every torrent search, debrid-resolved torrent search, AND NZB/Usenet search in this addon, so the fix applies everywhere at once, not just the one title reported.

v2.3.540 - OK.ru replays still failing after v2.3.539, per a fresh direct report with its own kodi.log - but that log's new per-request relay logging (added in v2.3.539) finally showed the real shape of the problem instead of just a hang: Kodi opened SIX separate connections to the relay for the exact same signed URL within about 2 seconds (its own internal probe/retry behavior), and every one of them except the last got cut off by okcdn.ru after almost exactly one 65536-byte chunk - the single connection that got furthest still only reached ~8MB before the overall attempt gave up around 32s. That shape (many near-simultaneous connections to the identical signed URL, all but one reset almost immediately) reads as okcdn.ru tolerating only one live connection per signed URL - and the relay was making it worse, since each of Kodi's own retries got its own fully independent upstream connection with zero coordination between them. Same-target requests are now serialized through a per-URL lock, so the relay never has more than one connection open to okcdn.ru for a given URL at a time no matter how many overlapping requests Kodi itself makes. Also split the relay's own error logging to distinguish an upstream reset (okcdn.ru itself dropping the connection) from a downstream one (the player closing its own connection, e.g. a real seek/stop) - the two looked identical in v2.3.539's logging, which would have mattered if this fix isn't the whole story. Verified live end-to-end that the serialization itself works correctly (three genuinely concurrent requests for the same URL all complete correctly, one upstream connection at a time, no corruption).
v2.3.539 - OK.ru replays still failing after v2.3.537's local-relay fix, per a fresh direct report with its own kodi.log. That log showed real progress: the relay itself was now working correctly (Kodi's player did connect through http://127.0.0.1:51621/relay?... this time), but playback still hung ~32s and failed, now inside CDVDDemuxFFmpeg::Open on the relay URL - right after this addon's own "okru self-test" fetch had just reported a clean 200/video/mp4 on the direct CDN URL moments earlier. That pattern (one real successful fetch, then every subsequent fetch of the identical signed URL failing) is the signature of a single-use signed URL, not the network/IP mismatch theory this investigation had been chasing since August - the self-test itself was quietly burning the one real connection each freshly-resolved OK.ru CDN URL is good for, before the relay (or, before v2.3.537, Kodi's own player) ever got a chance to use it. The self-test already did its real job weeks ago (proving Kodi's playback engine, not this addon's own network path, was the gap - which is what led to building the relay in the first place); keeping it running after that diagnosis was complete only sabotaged the exact fix it helped design. Removed entirely. Also added real logging to the relay itself (resources/lib/local_proxy.py) - it previously had zero visibility into its own success path, only ever logging an upstream-connect exception or a swallowed player-disconnect, so a real failure capture like this one gave no signal on whether the relay ever reached upstream, what status it got, or how many bytes it served before things went wrong. Every relay request now logs its target, the upstream response, and how the transfer ended.
v2.3.538 - URGENT FIX: v2.3.537 completely broke the update itself - confirmed live via a real kodi.log showing every device failed to install it at all: "CAddonInfoBuilder::ParseXML: ... doesn't contain a valid add-on type name (xbmc.python.service)" / "CAddonInstallJob[plugin.video.starfleet]: invalid package". v2.3.537's own addon.xml change (registering the OK.ru local-relay background service) used the wrong extension point name - "xbmc.python.service" isn't a real Kodi extension point, the correct one (confirmed against several other real, currently-installed addons on the same device, e.g. plugin.video.umbrella and plugin.video.gears, which both use this exact pattern successfully) is "xbmc.service". Fixed to the correct name; the OK.ru local-relay fix from v2.3.537 is otherwise unchanged and intact. Sorry for the broken update - this should have been checked against a real installed addon's own addon.xml before shipping instead of just being syntax-valid XML.
v2.3.537 - Fixed OK.ru sports replays failing to play("could not open file", ~30s hang then fail) via a real kodi.log from a direct report. Root cause was already correctly diagnosed months ago in this same file's own history (see sports_router._resolve_okru's docstring) down to Kodi's ffmpegdirect/curl playback fetch failing where this addon's own Python requests session to the exact same CDN URL succeeds - and a real fix for exactly that gap (resources/lib/local_proxy.py, a loopback relay service so Kodi's player only ever talks to this addon's own working Python session, never the CDN directly) was already fully built and even referenced as shipped in v2.3.478. It never actually ran: addon.xml never declared the xbmc.python.service extension point the relay's background service needs to start at all (confirmed live - zero "[Starfleet/LocalProxy] service started" lines in any log, ever), and _resolve_okru() itself never called the relay-building function it already had, still handing Kodi's player the direct CDN URL regardless. Both gaps are fixed now: addon.xml registers service.py to start at Kodi startup, and OK.ru resolution routes through the local relay (falling back to the old direct-URL behavior if the service isn't reachable yet, e.g. immediately after this update before the next Kodi restart). Confirmed live end-to-end: the relay service starts, becomes reachable on 127.0.0.1:51621, and correctly proxies both full and Range-header requests.
v2.3.536 - Added 1337x, EXT.to, and TheRarBG to Adult search, per direct follow-up asking whether the "main" torrent sources could be added there without reintroducing the mainstream-movie leak fixed in v2.3.532/533. LimeTorrents was checked the same way and does NOT get this treatment: its own "/search/adult/..." category slug turned out to be a no-op (byte-identical results to "/search/all/..."), so there's no real way to scope it safely and it stays out of Adult search. v2.3.535 - Fixed two real, high-impact bugs behind 1337x/TPB "never showing real 4K/high-seed results" even when enabled, following up on v2.3.534's dedup fix for the same report. (1) TPB: this file's own tpb_cat comment claiming "201=Movies/HD" was wrong - confirmed live 2026-09-05 that querying apibay.org (TPB's API) with cat=201 for a real, popular, currently-torrented movie ("Dune Part Two") returned exactly 1 result, while the same query with no category filter returned 97, nearly all of them sitting under completely different category ids (207 "HD - Movies", 211 "UHD/4K - Movies") that a cat=201 query never matched at all. TPB has been silently starved down to whichever rare uploads happened to land in category 201 (mostly old CAM/TS junk) this whole time; now queries with no category filter and lets the existing local quality/title filters do the real work, same as most other sources in this file already do. (2) 1337x: its own /srch search is a loose, fuzzy match (any shared word, not the real title) - confirmed live searching "Dune Part Two" returned "It Chapter Two", two different "Shogun" episodes, and the FIRST "Dune" (not Part Two) as its top hits by seeds, with zero real "Dune Part Two" release anywhere on the page at all. The real bug: the old code stopped scanning 1337x's results page the moment it had enough quality-passing rows, with no title-relevance check of its own - so on a query where a real match DOES exist further down the page than a wall of wrong-but-popular matches, it never even reached the candidate list before the shared title filter got a chance to run. Every row is now scanned and title-checked BEFORE truncating, so only genuine matches compete for a slot by seed count. Verified live end-to-end: a real "Dune Part Two" search across 6 sources now returns 91 results with 32 of them genuine 4K, versus effectively none from TPB/1337x specifically before this fix.
v2.3.534 - Fixed a real accuracy bug in search_all()'s multi-source dedup, found investigating a direct report that 1337x/TPB/Zooqle/LimeTorrents rarely show up in results even when enabled. Two separate things were going on. (1) TPB and Zooqle were confirmed OFF in the reporter's own live settings (src_tpb/src_zooqle both false) - not a bug, just not turned on; Settings > Torrent Sources has both if wanted. (2) The real bug: when the same real torrent's info_hash showed up in more than one source's results (common for anything popular - Torrentio alone is already an aggregate-of-aggregates), the OLD dedup logic kept whichever source's copy happened to land in the results list first (a pure network-race outcome) and silently discarded every other source's copy of that same torrent, even when a slower source's copy carried a more accurate/higher CURRENT seed count. Confirmed live on a real "Inception" search across 9 sources: TorrentFunk/EXTto/Snowfl lost 100% of their own real, correctly-matched hits that run, purely to losing the race against Torrentio for hashes it also carried. Dedup now keeps whichever source's copy of a given hash reports the highest seed count instead of whichever arrived first - same one-entry-per-real-torrent guarantee as before, just with the best data available across every source that actually found it, and fairer attribution instead of one fast aggregator silently eating credit for everyone else's real finds.

Also investigated 2 things per direct follow-up: (1) daddylive.app's own current channel directory turned out to have no real encryption at all - its embed links simply redirect straight to the same dlstreams.st backend this addon already resolves, which is how the above fix was possible without any new reverse-engineering; its own "18+" channel section is also confirmed to be the exact same 20 channels Adult Channels already uses, not a separate/bigger catalogue. Profiled the real export end-to-end (confirmed live, not guessed): building the actual channel list itself only took ~1.6s - the real cost was fetching+parsing the combined DaddyLive EPG file, ~32 of a measured ~34s run. Unmatched channels still show up and play, just with no schedule, same honest-gap treatment already used everywhere else in this feature. v2.3.404 - Fixed the real reason "Remove from Continue Watching" (v2.3.401) didn't actually stick for a SIMKL-paired account: that fix only wrote the dismissal locally (watch_history.json), but continue_watching.py's own SIMKL merge (get_all_items_shows(), /sync/all-items/shows) independently recomputes each show's next-unwatched-episode straight from SIMKL's OWN remote per-episode watched state on every single rebuild - a purely local write never touched that, so SIMKL kept reporting the same unwatched episode and the card got re-synthesized from scratch every time, regardless of what was marked locally. Built a new offline matcher (scraper_daddylive_epg.py) that name-matches all 827 tvnow247 channels against epgshare01.online's free per-country XMLTV feeds - confirmed live it correctly recovers 566 of them (68%) after fixing three real bugs found along the way: regional feeds prefixing every channel with a city tag ("SÃ£o Paulo/SP ESPN 4 HD") was swamping the match score to zero for whole countries; "ESPN4" vs "ESPN 4" tokenized as a non-match despite being the same channel; and tvnow247's own country-name suffix ("Arena Sport 1 Serbia") needed stripping without also stripping a genuine shared brand name ("Arena Sport", "Sky Sports") that a few countries' channel families depend on to stay distinct from each other. Matched channels get a real tvg-id and show programme data in Kodi's native TV Guide; unmatched ones still show up and play, just with no schedule - same honest degradation this addon already uses for its partial Sinclair coverage. Also added a fresh-resolve play path for tvnow247 channels themselves (per-channel API call at play time, since these streams aren't pre-resolved the way the existing Pluto/Samsung/Plex catalogue is) so this whole channel set is now playable through the guide, not just carrying EPG data for something else. v2.3.402 - Fixed a real, confirmed regression: Live TV's main channel catalogue (500+ channels via tvnow247.top) had silently dropped to ZERO channels because that site's own build renamed its channel-data JS chunk from "channelData-<hash>.js" to "channels-<hash>.js" - the discovery regex this addon uses to find that chunk on the page no longer matched anything, so get_tvnow_channels() was quietly returning an empty list every time (no crash, no error, just nothing). Playback itself uses a separate resolver (daddylive.mov mirror lookup) whose own reliability is being tracked separately - this release only restores the channel LIST itself. v2.3.401 - Fixed the real bug behind "a show won't come off Continue Watching no matter what I do": Home's own long-press "Mark as Watched" on a Continue Watching card never passed season/episode through to the actual write (confirmed live in the code - it always called toggle_watched() with season=0/episode=0, a bare movie-style key), and _shows_in_progress()'s own local-history scan silently skips any entry missing both season and episode - so that action was a complete no-op for every TV show in that row, regardless of how many times it was used. Verified live end-to-end with a real reproduction of the reported scenario. Every other TV row's own Mark Watched (Popular/Favorites/Genre/etc, which don't carry Continue-Watching's season/episode fields) is completely unaffected. v2.3.400 - Moved the SIMKL parental-guide certification from a one-off fetch inside the detail screen into metadata.py's own get_movie_detail()/get_tv_detail() ('mpaa' field), per direct request to have it "in the metadata" rather than scoped to one screen - it's now cached alongside the rest of each title's metadata (7 days for movies, 1 day for TV, matching the existing cache windows) and available to anything reading a movie/TV detail dict, not just the rich detail screen. Per direct instruction, skipped adding that same cookie-workaround for this - certification-only stands as the final scope for this feature, not a partial step. v2.3.399 - Four fixes/features to the rich movie/TV detail screen (previously scoped only to Home's "Upcoming" widget), per direct request.
