Search hits the site's own JSON API, which conveniently returns each show's real imdb_id directly - preferred over fuzzy title matching when available, more reliable than any other scraper in this file. The specific episode's URL is built directly from the show's slug + season/episode (confirmed live: predictable, no need to page through the show's own episode grid), then its obfuscated embed-host links are decoded with the same offset-cipher algorithm the cMaN-repo "TV Free" addon uses for this same site, verified against a real decoded episode page rather than assumed from that addon's code alone. Returns 30+ real hoster links per episode (Vidmoly, Streamtape, Voe, Doodstream, Mixdrop, etc.) straight into the existing ResolveURL-backed source picker, same as every other scraper in this file. v2.3.397 - Closed the one real gap left in SIMKL Continue Watching merging: a show with watched episodes on SIMKL but nothing currently paused there (the last episode already crossed SIMKL's own completion threshold, or was watched via a device/app - e.g. a different Kodi addon - that never sent a scrobble/pause at all) previously didn't show up here even though there was clearly more to watch. Confirmed live and wired up GET /sync/all-items/shows, which SIMKL already uses to compute each show's own "next episode to watch" from its per-episode watched state - no local TMDB catalog walk needed for a show that was never touched on this device at all. Also fixed a real off-by-one this surfaced: the existing SIMKL merge's anchor calculation broke specifically when the next episode to watch was Episode 1 itself (season 1 or any season) - it would incorrectly treat that first episode as already "anchored past" and skip straight to episode 2. Both this new merge tier and the existing one share the fix. v2.3.396 - Three fixes/features around Adult content and SIMKL, per direct request. (1) Confirmed and fixed a real bug: adult playback's internal ids (e.g. "ade:5122655") were passed through the exact same code path as real content and would have been sent to a paired SIMKL account as a bogus IMDB id - simkl_sync.py now only ever sends something shaped like a genuine IMDB id (tt<digits>), so adult content never reaches SIMKL, period, independent of any setting. (2) Added a new "Track adult watched/resume progress" toggle (Settings > Adult Section, OFF by default) - local resume position/watched-checkmark/Continue-Watching tracking for Adult content now only happens if explicitly turned on; manual Mark Watched/Unwatched from a favorites list still works regardless, since that's a deliberate organizational action, not automatic tracking. (3) Successfully pairing a SIMKL account now asks whether to wipe this device's own local movie/TV watch progress so SIMKL becomes the sole source of truth for Continue Watching going forward - adult progress is never touched by this prompt either way. Also manually cleared this session's own local watch_history.json of 12 stale near-zero-progress test entries left over from before SIMKL pairing existed (backed up first), confirming along the way that the SIMKL cross-device merge built in v2.3.391 genuinely works end-to-end: P-Valley showed up in Continue Watching with zero local record on this device at all, purely from a real SIMKL /sync/playback session. v2.3.395 - Added a new "Buy Me a Coffee" Settings section, per direct request: one button per coin (BTC, ETH, DOGE, BCH, LTC, XRP) shows a QR code for the author's own deposit address, with an optional donor-typed amount pre-filled into the QR via each coin's own standard URI format (BIP21 for BTC/DOGE/BCH/LTC, EIP-681 for ETH's wei value). LINK was deliberately left out - it's an ERC-20 token sharing ETH's deposit address, but a correct amount-prefilled URI for it needs the token's own contract address encoded a completely different way, which wasn't confirmed safe to build blind. XRP always displays its required destination tag as its own large, high-contrast line regardless of whether the donor's wallet honors the amount/tag in the URI, since a dropped tag can misdirect a deposit on the receiving exchange's end. No obligation either way - entirely optional, address-display only, no accounts or pairing involved. v2.3.394 - Three things, per direct request: (1) Continue Watching's "next episode hasn't aired yet" case is no longer hidden entirely - it now shows the show with a distinct red-italic "New episode airs <date>" line in the hero banner instead of the usual year/rating (Kodi labels support [COLOR]/[I] markup directly in the text, so this needed no skin XML changes), and clicking it shows a clean "not aired yet" notification instead of trying to play something that doesn't exist yet. (2) You can now long-press a SEASON itself in the season picker and choose "Mark Season as Watched / Unwatched" to toggle every episode in it at once, instead of one episode at a time - if the season is only partially watched, this marks everything watched (not unwatched) first; a second long-press unmarks the whole thing. (3) Proactively applied the same fresh-Addon()-instance fix from v2.3.392's TMDB bug to SIMKL pairing too (simkl_auth.py/simkl_sync.py) - confirmed SIMKL itself was never actually paired on the device this was tested on (its access token was still completely unset in the real settings.xml), so the "Continue Watching still only shows local content" report wasn't a bug at all - there was nothing paired for it to merge with yet - but the identical stale-settings-cache bug existed in SIMKL's own pairing check too and would have caused the exact same silent failure the moment someone did pair it mid-session, so it's fixed now regardless. v2.3.392 - Fixed the real reason TMDB Favorites still weren't writing to the list even after pairing successfully, root-caused via kodi.log timestamps: settings.xml showed the paired token written to disk a full 9 seconds BEFORE a same-session "Remove from Favorites" call still read it as unpaired. Cause: this addon's Home screen runs as one long-lived Python process for the whole session, and favorites.py held a single xbmcaddon.Addon() object constructed once when that process started - a well-known Kodi gotcha where an Addon() instance can freeze whatever settings looked like at construction time, so pairing done afterward (a separate, freshly-spawned Settings action) never got picked up by the already-running Home process no matter how long you waited. Fixed by constructing a fresh Addon() on every settings read instead of reusing one held for the whole session; verified with a standalone test reproducing the exact real scenario (settings written by one process, read by an already-running one) both broken before and fixed after. Also fixed two more real bugs from testing the TMDB pairing dialog live: the QR code was rendering roughly 1.5x larger than intended (a wrong assumption that Kodi's Python window coordinates match real screen pixels 1:1 - they're actually always a fixed 1280x720 virtual space Kodi scales to the real display), and the status line was overwriting itself with a duplicate of the instruction text every few seconds instead of a real status update. TMDB pairing now also shows a proper QR code (previously a raw, un-typeable 100+ character URL as plain text) via a new shared resources/lib/gui/qr_dialog.py module, reused by SIMKL pairing too. v2.3.391 - Per direct request: the Home carousel's Continue Watching row now merges across devices too, not just resume-seek position (v2.3.389). When SIMKL is paired, GET /sync/playback is folded into both the movies and TV-shows halves of the row two ways - (1) a title already showing here whose SIMKL-saved progress is further along than what this device itself recorded gets its displayed percentage/next-episode bumped to match, so two paired devices show the same numbers, not just the same row; (2) a title with ZERO local record on this device at all, but genuinely in progress on another device per SIMKL, gets synthesized into the row from scratch (fresh TMDB lookup for its poster/title) so it shows up here even though this device has never played a second of it. Verified with a standalone test covering all of these cases plus the one that matters most: with no SIMKL account paired, the row is byte-for-byte the same as it's always been - nothing about this changes anything for anyone not using SIMKL. One known, deliberately unaddressed gap: a title fully finished on another device with nothing currently paused, and zero local record here, won't be excluded from (or added to) this row - that needs SIMKL's full watched-history endpoint, whose exact response shape wasn't confirmed with enough confidence via its docs to build on yet, unlike /sync/playback which was verified live before any of this was written. v2.3.390 - Fixed the SIMKL pairing QR dialog from v2.3.388 being nearly unreadable, confirmed live via a real screenshot: it was a plain WindowDialog with no background of its own at all, so whatever screen was open behind it (the Settings list, in the report) showed straight through and visually interlaced with the code/instructions text. Gave it a real opaque background panel (reusing this addon's own existing white.png tintable texture, the same technique Starfleet-Progress.xml already uses elsewhere), and split the pairing code onto its own large, letter-spaced, high-contrast line separate from the smaller "go to this URL" instructional text, instead of one small line sharing space with everything else. v2.3.389 - Real cross-device watch-progress sync via SIMKL, the actual payoff of v2.3.388's pairing work: pausing/stopping a title on one device now saves its exact position to your paired SIMKL account (POST /scrobble/start when playback begins, /scrobble/pause or /scrobble/stop - whichever matches SIMKL's own 80%-watched threshold - when it ends), and a DIFFERENT device opening the same title checks GET /sync/playback before playback starts and resumes from whichever position is furthest along, local or remote. Verified with a standalone test harness against the confirmed SIMKL API shapes (exact request bodies for movies vs TV episodes, exact matching logic against a fake /sync/playback response) and the merge logic (remote ahead of local -> adopt it; remote behind local -> keep local; remote already >=90% -> ignored as effectively finished, not treated as a resume point). One real, unavoidable limitation, called out honestly rather than papered over: SIMKL stores progress as a percentage, not seconds, so turning it back into a resume point needs a known total duration - the very first time a title is ever played on a given device, there's nothing to multiply that percentage against yet, so remote progress is skipped rather than guessed at; from the second time that title is played on that device onward (once a local duration exists either way), remote progress from any other device becomes usable. Entirely no-op, exactly as before, if no SIMKL account is paired. This was NOT possible via Trakt: confirmed live that Trakt's own equivalent (sync/playback) sits behind a free-tier connected-app limit as of this month, one of the two reasons (the other being the pairing-friction fix in v2.3.388) this was built on SIMKL instead. v2.3.388 - SIMKL pairing (Settings > Premium Services) is now as easy as debrid pairing, per direct request: removed the manual "paste a SIMKL Client ID" step the same way v2.3.387 removed it for TMDB - bundled one real, verified client_id into the addon (same shared-app model, doesn't grant access to anyone's account, every user still personally approves their own account during pairing). "Pair with SIMKL" now also shows a real QR code (via pyqrcode, the same library ResolveURL's own debrid pairing already uses, confirmed already installed as a dependency) next to the short code, so pairing is scan-and-approve on a phone instead of typing anything on a Firestick remote - falls back to the existing plain-text code dialog automatically if QR generation isn't available for any reason. This is prep work for the next step: real cross-device watch-progress sync via SIMKL's scrobble/resume API (confirmed live this exists and is free, unlike Trakt's now-paywalled multi-app connections) - not wired up yet, pairing is the first piece. v2.3.387 - Removed the manual "paste your TMDB API Read Access Token" step from v2.3.386's TMDB pairing (Settings > Favorites): that was correctly flagged as painful, especially on a device you don't have a real keyboard for - typing a 40+ character token via a Firestick remote is brutal, and it would have had to be repeated on every separate device. Fixed by bundling one real, verified token into the addon itself (same shared-app model already used for years by this addon's own TMDB_KEYS in metadata.py, which every Starfleet install already shares for search/metadata without exposing anyone's account) - it only identifies "this is the Starfleet app" during the handshake, it does not grant access to any account's data. Every user still personally logs into their own TMDB account and approves in their own browser during pairing, getting their own separate access_token, and still points at their own TMDB List ID in Settings exactly as before - none of that changed. "Pair with TMDB" is now a single click plus a browser approval, no typing required, on any device. v2.3.386 - Answered a direct question with a real feature: holding OK to add/remove a Favorite can now WRITE straight to your TMDB List (Settings > Favorites), not just read one. Confirmed live against TMDB's actual API before building this: their simpler v3 write endpoint is movie-only by design (it's literally named "Add Movie"/"Remove Movie" in TMDB's own reference, no way to pass a TV item through it at all), so since this addon's Favorites already deliberately mix movies and TV in one list, real write support needed TMDB's separate v4 auth system instead - a personal "API Read Access Token (v4 auth)" from your own themoviedb.org account (Settings > API), pasted into a new field, then a "Pair with TMDB" button that walks through TMDB's own request-token-then-approve-in-browser flow (mirrors this addon's existing Trakt pairing) and stores the resulting access token. Once paired, holding OK writes/removes items on the real TMDB List immediately (verified against TMDB's actual request/response shapes for all 4 endpoints involved: request_token, access_token, list add, list remove) and clears this device's own 30-minute list cache so the change shows up right away instead of waiting out the cache. Without pairing, a configured List ID still works exactly as before - read-only, with a toast pointing at themoviedb.org. v2.3.385 - Replaced the single blanket "search additional slower torrent sources" toggle from v2.3.383 with a full "Torrent Sources" settings category (Settings, new category between General and Premium Services): every one of the ~35 torrent scrapers now has its own individual on/off toggle, so a user who wants one specific slower source (e.g. Nyaa for anime, or TorrentFunk) no longer has to turn all ~20 of them on just to get it. The 15 core/fast sources (aggregator APIs + Knaben/TPB/YTS/EZTV/1337x) still default on exactly as v2.3.383 shipped; the ~20 slower single-site scrapers still default off. Two buttons cover the all-or-nothing cases without clicking through every toggle by hand: "Enable All Sources" and "Reset to Recommended (Fast) Set". search_all()'s 15-minute result cache key now accounts for which sources are actually enabled, so toggling settings doesn't return a stale mix from before the change. Directly implements the request to keep the top sources always active by default while letting users pick their own preferred mix individually or in bulk. v2.3.384 - Fixed a real bug reported live: picking a DoodStream (Adult section) source sometimes tried to play a completely broken page instead of failing cleanly. Confirmed via kodi.log: DoodStream is currently behind a real Cloudflare challenge neither Starfleet's own resolver nor ResolveURL can solve (nothing to fix there, it's a genuine site-side wall) - but adult_stream_play()'s own fallback check only ever caught ONE specific failure shape (an unresolved JS embed whose URL happens to contain a "#"), so a hoster ResolveURL recognized but failed to resolve for any OTHER reason fell through and got handed to Kodi's player as if it were a real result, which of course failed to open with a 403. Now any hoster ResolveURL recognizes as needing resolution that doesn't actually resolve reports a clean "Could not resolve stream" notification instead. Also confirmed via a live log that v2.3.383's source-count trim IS working correctly (only ~14 sources ran instead of ~34) - the remaining perceived slowness on that particular run was several of the core sources (Knaben, TPB, YTS, DMM, Zilean) hitting real, live connection timeouts, not sheer source count. Lowered the overall per-search ceiling from 25s to 18s (matching gears' own ~20s external-search cap) so a run with a few genuinely slow/down sources doesn't drag the whole search out as long, at the modest cost of occasionally cutting off a slow-but-would-have-succeeded source. v2.3.383 - Fixed a real, confirmed bug reported live: picking a Comet-sourced result sometimes played a completely different episode than requested. Root cause was systemic across ALL FOUR debrid services, not specific to Comet - Comet just surfaces season-pack magnets (one file per episode) more often than other sources. Every *_magnet_to_stream function picked a file with zero regard for which episode it actually was: Real-Debrid took links[0] (whatever RD returned first), AllDebrid/Premiumize picked "the single biggest video file in the whole torrent", TorBox hardcoded file_id=0 - all four could easily hand back a different episode than the one that was actually requested from a real season pack, even though the torrent itself was genuinely the correct show. Fixed by filtering each service's own file list down to the one matching the requested season/episode (via each file's own S/E marker) before picking - the same principle already used correctly elsewhere in this addon for the user's own AllDebrid library matches, just missing from the live-search path. Movies and single-episode releases are unaffected (nothing to disambiguate). Also, per direct request: trimmed torrent_sources.search_all() to a fast core set by default (aggregator APIs + Knaben/TPB/YTS/EZTV/1337x) - the ~20 slower single-site HTML/CF-walled scrapers that were the main reason a Starfleet search ran noticeably longer than gears' equivalent for comparable results are now opt-in only (Settings > General > "Search additional slower torrent sources"), off by default. v2.3.382 - Fixed a real regression from v2.3.381's native-DialogProgress reversion: reported live as metadata/artwork loading feeling slower across the whole addon, not just NZB resolution. Root cause: that reversion changed the DEFAULT progress dialog for every single call site in the addon (confirmed ~40+ of them, including home.py's own carousel/widget/metadata loading spinners) from the addon's own custom-skinned dialog to Kodi's native one - and native DialogProgress means a real skin context-switch to the user's system skin (Estuary) and back every single time it's shown, which used to only cost something on the 2 flows that actually need a working Cancel (NZB/slow-magnet resolution), and now cost it everywhere. Scoped correctly this time: the custom, fast, no-skin-switch dialog is back as the default for the ~40 general "loading..." spinners across the addon (home.py, router.py, afdb_router.py, etc.), where Cancel not being fully reliable is a minor nicety, not a real problem given how short those operations are - only the 2 call sites that genuinely need working Cancel during a multi-minute wait (NZB resolution, slow magnet resolution in resolvers.py) still use the native dialog. v2.3.381 - Cancel STILL didn't actually work on the NZB progress dialog after v2.3.380's rewrite - confirmed live via a real report and a kodi.log trace showing a "cancelled" download survive 16+ minutes (including a full sleep/wake cycle) and finish anyway. Two different custom themed-dialog implementations (show()-based, then doModal()-on-a-background-thread) both failed on the same thing: clicks on the Cancel button never reliably reached Python at all, even though the dialog visibly rendered and updated correctly both times. Reverted this one dialog to Kodi's own native xbmcgui.DialogProgress() - the actual built-in mechanism this "background work + real cancel" pattern is designed for, guaranteed to route input correctly since it's not a custom window competing for focus. Costs the navy/orange theming on this one dialog (falls back to the system skin's own progress look); every call site needed zero changes. Also: investigated why gears' scraper feels faster/finds more and implemented the 2 biggest wins found - (1) torrent_sources.search_all() was never cached at all (confirmed: the ~30+ live sources got re-hit from scratch on every single search, even an immediate repeat of the same title/episode) - now cached 15 minutes, so retries/autoplay-next-episode/reopening the source picker are instant instead of paying the full sweep again; (2) trimmed the outer "debrid branch" search budget in the picker from 110s to 60s (the internal source-search itself is already capped at 25s; 110s was leaving up to nearly 2 minutes of headroom for what should be at most a high-outlier ~45s including the small fixed-cost lookups around it - gears' equivalent phase is hard-capped at 20s). v2.3.380 - Fixed two more real, confirmed-live NZB bugs. (1) Cancel on the NZB progress dialog never actually worked at all, in any version, not just "was slow" - traced to the dialog being shown via show() (non-blocking) while running its own poll loop on the same thread; confirmed live that this leaves the window visually updating (progress/ETA text moving) but never actually receiving click input at all - no onClick, no onAction, ever, even after several real minutes of watching it. Rebuilt the dialog to run via doModal() on its own background thread instead, which actually grants it real input focus - Cancel now closes it immediately, verified live. No call sites (magnet resolution, NZB resolution) needed to change, since this lived entirely inside the shared dialog helper. (2) Wrong file played after picking an NZB: confirmed live picking "Lioness S03E01" instead played an unrelated 2026 movie ("The Death of Robin Hood") that happened to still be sitting in Premiumize's account. Root cause: Premiumize dumps every NZB upload's resulting file into ONE SHARED destination folder in the account, not an isolated per-transfer folder - "play the biggest video file in that folder" (this addon's only signal until now) can and did grab a bigger, completely unrelated leftover from an earlier, different search instead of the correct smaller file that was also right there. Fixed by filtering the shared folder's contents by the actual title/season/episode being searched for (the exact same precision matcher already used for torrent results) before picking the biggest match - if nothing in the folder actually matches, this now correctly reports nothing playable instead of guessing. v2.3.379 - Fixed Cancel not working on the NZB download progress dialog (confirmed live on a real 9.9GB 4K release with a 53-minute ETA - clicking Cancel had no visible effect). Root cause: the polling loop only checked whether the user had cancelled once per ~10-second Premiumize API poll, right after that poll's own network call finished - clicking Cancel could sit unacknowledged for the full 10s poll interval plus however long the in-flight request itself was still waiting on, easily 20-30+ seconds of apparent unresponsiveness on a slow response. Decoupled the two: the dialog now re-checks for cancellation every 1 second using the last known status (no network call), while the actual Premiumize poll still only runs every ~10s so it doesn't hammer their API - Cancel now takes effect within about a second regardless of how slow any individual API response is. Also raised the outer time cap for very large/slow NZB downloads (confirmed live one real 4K release estimated 53 minutes) from 20 to 60 minutes, so a legitimately slow but progressing download doesn't get cut off as if it were stuck. v2.3.378 - Root-caused and fixed why NZB results never actually played on Premiumize even after picking one from the list (v2.3.377's fix only made picking one attempt to resolve at all - it still failed silently every time). Confirmed live: Premiumize's directdl endpoint (the same one used for magnet caching) flatly rejects Binsearch's/NZBGeek's/NZBPlanet's own NZB download links with "Unsupported link for direct download" - it can't recognize a dynamically-generated action URL as a valid NZB source by shape alone, even though that exact URL serves a perfectly valid .nzb file when fetched directly (verified). Also discovered along the way: unlike magnet caching (an instant check against a shared cache of already-downloaded torrents), Premiumize has NO shared cache for Usenet content at all - resolving an NZB is a genuine real-time download from Usenet on Premiumize's own end, confirmed live taking over a minute for a real ~3GB episode. Fixed by fetching the actual .nzb file bytes ourselves and uploading them directly to Premiumize (multipart, via transfer/create - confirmed live this is correctly recognized), then polling until the real download finishes and reading back the actual playable link - verified end-to-end against two different real episodes, both resolved to genuine playable stream URLs. Since this is a real multi-minute wait rather than an instant lookup, NZB resolution now shows the same kind of progress dialog (with cancel) magnet resolution already has, surfacing Premiumize's own real download progress instead of looking like a silent hang. v2.3.377 - EMERGENCY FIX for v2.3.376: the new NZB title filter rejected 100% of results, every single search, confirmed live via kodi.log ("Title filter removed 10 false matches" / "10 -> 0 candidates", repeated across 3 different unrelated searches). Root cause: Binsearch wraps its raw titles in quote characters, and unlike torrent titles (which never have them), a leading quote glued directly onto the first word (e.g. "the odyssey...) turned that word into its own token the filter's prefix-check didn't recognize as skippable, rejecting every candidate regardless of content the moment the new filter started running against them. Fixed by stripping quote characters (straight and curly/smart) to spaces during normalization, same as every other punctuation character already is - verified directly: the exact quote-wrapped case that broke it now survives correctly, and the original garbage-title rejection (Virgin River/Happy Tree Friends/etc from the v2.3.376 fix) still works exactly as before. v2.3.376 - Fixed NZB search (Movies/TV) returning completely unrelated shows mixed in with real results: confirmed live (user screenshot) that searching "Found S01E03" returned "Virgin River S01E03", "Happy Tree Friends S01E03", "Eyes of Wakanda S01E03" etc alongside the real match, because Binsearch/Newznab search is a loose multi-word match (any result containing similar terms, not an exact title match) and NZB results never went through the same strict title+episode filter every torrent source already does. Extracted that filter (previously inline only in torrent_sources.py's search_all()) into its own reusable function and now applies it to NZB candidates too - verified directly against the exact garbage titles from the report: all correctly rejected, only the real match survives. Also added the same NZB-resolution fix shipped for Movies/TV in v2.3.375 to the Adult section's own separate play path (afdb_router.py's adult_stream_play()), which had an identical gap - picking an NZB result there would also try to play the raw NZB link directly instead of resolving it through Premiumize/TorBox first. v2.3.375 - Fixed NZB results (Movies/TV, Premiumize/TorBox enabled) not actually playing: confirmed live via kodi.log a real crash (CDVDDemuxFFmpeg failing to probe a raw binsearch.info search-page URL handed straight to the player) - root cause was in the picker-building code (metadata_router.py), which rebuilds every debrid search result into a fresh dict for display, but that rebuild dropped the 'is_nzb' flag NZB candidates need, so picking one silently skipped the Premiumize/TorBox resolution step entirely and tried to play the raw NZB search link as if it were a video file. Also fixed why NZB results never showed a quality tag/filter the way torrent results do: their picker label was built from just source name + file size ("[NZB] Binsearch 2.3GB"), never the actual release title - and the picker's quality sort scans label TEXT for tags like 1080p/WEB-DL, so a label with no title in it can never match anything. NZB labels now include the real release title, so real 4K/1080p/etc releases sort and display correctly like everything else. v2.3.374 - Fixed the debrid "Pair Device" buttons (Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/Premiumize/TorBox, Settings > Premium Services): confirmed live via kodi.log that clicking one crashed outright ("TypeError: function takes at most 2 arguments (4 given)" - this Kodi's DialogProgress.update() only accepts (percent, message), not the 4-argument form the first version of this feature assumed), and even fixed, that version would only ever show plain text, not the actual QR code the user pointed out gears'/ResolveURL's own pairing flow shows. Root cause of the whole approach: gears itself has zero debrid-pairing code of its own (confirmed by reading its full installed source) - what looks like "gears' pairing" is really just script.module.resolveurl's own separate Settings > Authorize My Account flow, which Starfleet already depends on (see addon.xml's own required import). Rewritten to call straight into ResolveURL's own resolver classes' authorize_resolver() method for each service, reusing its exact, already-proven QR-code-plus-short-code-plus-countdown dialog verbatim instead of reimplementing any of it - verified live just now: clicking Pair Device now shows a real QR code, a 4-character code, the goto URL, and a live countdown with no crash, and the resulting token is copied into Starfleet's own native API-key setting once authorized. v2.3.373 - Added NZBGeek and NZBPlanet as NZB search sources (Settings, new fields under Premium Services) for users with their own paid accounts at either site - both speak the standard Newznab API, verified live against each with a placeholder key (correct, standard "invalid API key" XML error back from both, confirming the request shape is right). v2.3.372 - Added a device-pairing button for Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/Premiumize/TorBox as an alternative to manually pasting an API key (later found buggy and superseded by v2.3.374 above). Also: researched and reported honestly on several other potential free NZB/torrent sources (RuTracker, showRSS, TorrentGalaxyClone, NZBKing, NZBIndex, FindNZB, NZBFriends) - most were dead ends (CSRF walls, client-rendered JS, expired domains, dead origin servers) and were not wired in. v2.3.371 - Usenet/NZB search (via binsearch.info, no account needed) is now gated to only run when Premiumize or TorBox is enabled - confirmed live that Real-Debrid and AllDebrid have no NZB/Usenet support at all, so searching NZB sources with neither of the two that do enabled would only ever waste time for no possible result. v2.3.350 - Added adultdvdparadise.org as a new free adult stream source (adult_streams.py), merged into the same "free stream" library as freeomovie.to/pornwatch.ws/watchpornfree.info (per direct request checking a list of 5 candidate sites - 3 were already in: freeomovie.to, pornwatch.ws, watchpornfree.info; paradisehill.cc was not investigated this round). Confirmed live it runs the exact same WordPress DooPlay theme + dooplayer plugin as pornwatch.ws, so its detail pages carry the identical data-fl-url stream attribute pointing at Doodstream links - reused pornwatch's own stream-extraction regex unchanged. The only real difference is the listing-page markup: this site runs WP Fastest Cache Premium, which lazy-loads every thumbnail behind a blank placeholder image and stashes the real URL in a different attribute, so the card-parsing regex needed its own version. Verified live: page 1 returns 9 real films, each resolving 8-10 working Doodstream links. v2.3.349 - Fixed a real, confirmed data-loss bug reported live: watch/resume progress (watch_history.json) could be silently and permanently erased. Root cause, traced back to v2.3.346's since-fixed CPU-starvation bug (see v2.3.347): if Kodi ever killed a hung/slow script process mid-write (exactly what that bug could cause), the write could be left truncated - invalid JSON. The next time ANYTHING tried to load the file, a parse error was silently swallowed and treated as "no history at all", and the very next play event would then save that empty state right back over the file, permanently wiping every real entry that was otherwise still sitting there past a single broken byte. Fixed two ways: (1) writes are now atomic (write to a temp file, then one atomic rename onto the real path) so a mid-write kill can never leave a truncated file in the first place; (2) if a corrupt file is ever encountered anyway, it's now backed up alongside the fresh empty one instead of being silently discarded, and logged as an error instead of an easy-to-miss warning. Verified live: a deliberately truncated file is now preserved as a .corrupt-TIMESTAMP backup rather than being overwritten into oblivion, and normal playback/resume tracking continues working immediately after. v2.3.348 - Added mythav.org as a fourth JAV source (mythav_sources.py), same pattern as javseen.tv/javhd.today/javleak.com. Its /update/ page is a flat, paginated "every new upload" feed, no sitemap needed. Detail pages embed a single iframe whose src is a base64-encoded upload18.org play-page URL; that page embeds a plain (non-obfuscated) JS config object whose "m3u8" field is a fully-signed, directly playable helvid.com HLS stream - confirmed live against 5 separate titles, no resolvers.py hand-off needed at all (unlike the other 3 JAV sources, this one's own chain already ends in a real stream). Also investigated and rejected javgiga.com: looked promising at first (one sample had a static resolvable iframe using the same hgcloud.to host javleak.com already uses), but a wider sample (7 pages total) showed that was a fluke - the real mechanism on nearly every page is a WordPress plugin that lazy-loads the video via a POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, and that specific endpoint sits behind a genuine Cloudflare challenge that even this addon's own vendored cloudscraper library couldn't get past. Not shippable as a reliable source, so it's not included. v2.3.347 - URGENT PERFORMANCE FIX for v2.3.346's hoofoot.ru addition, reported live: the whole addon (widget loading, other scraping, even watched/unwatched status writes) became sluggish or stuck after browsing sports, only recovering after a full reload. Root cause: the pure-Python AES-128-CBC decrypt written for hoofoot.ru's API (resources/lib/aes128.py) was a tight, CPU-bound loop with almost no I/O, so it holds Python's GIL almost continuously for as long as it runs - measured at 8+ seconds on a desktop PC for one real events payload, and a Firestick's much weaker CPU could easily push that to 60-120+ seconds. For that entire stretch, EVERY other Python thread in the addon (widgets, other scrapers, watched-status writes) stalls too, since it's a single process under one GIL - not just the sports code that actually needed the decrypt. Fixed by precomputing the 4 GF(256) multiplication tables InvMixColumns needs (previously an 8-iteration bit-loop per multiply, now an O(1) table lookup) and flattening the AES state representation - cuts real-payload decrypt time from 8.2s to 0.42s on the same test (~20x), re-verified correct against live hoofoot.ru data after the change. Same decrypted output, same behavior, just fast enough to no longer stall the rest of the addon while it runs. v2.3.346 - Added hoofoot.ru as a new sports source (sports_sources.py) - live in-addon, no Playwright needed. Its /api/events and /api/main-server endpoints look locked behind AES encryption, but the site's own schedule.js ships the decryption key in plain text (a static AES-128-CBC key, no key exchange at all). Since Kodi's bundled Python has no pycryptodome/cryptography to decrypt with, added a small hand-rolled pure-Python AES-128-CBC module (resources/lib/aes128.py) just for this. Decrypted event data maps to a YouTube embed or a same-domain URL that is already a real, directly playable HLS stream (confirmed live against real matches, both channel types). Covers tennis, soccer, MLB, handball, NBA, NHL, cricket, volleyball, cycling, golf, snooker, and UFC/MMA as its own primary event-listing source (same pattern as StreamsEast/MethStreams), with everything else it carries (Watersports, Softball, Horse Racing, Other) folded into the existing Other/International catch-all instead of dropped. Investigated the same night: streamiz.lol/firstrow (previously flagged for possible building-in) turned out to already be fully covered - it's a thin wrapper around livetv902.me, which sports_sources.py already has a complete, working resolver for (built in an earlier session, re-verified live tonight) - no new work needed there. v2.3.345 - Added FalconStreams.app as a new sports source (mlb, wnba, wwe, soccer, and more). Its homepage already lists every match's full data including a resolved stream list in one fetch, no extra page load needed - same standalone-scraper-plus-Playwright architecture as TotalSportek and DaddyLive (scraper_falconstreams.py), since its streams resolve through embed.st the same way those two already do. Confirmed live end-to-end against a real match: resolves to a genuine, directly playable stream link. v2.3.344 - Added TimStreams.st as a new USA Live TV source (11 channels: ABC, ACC Network, A&E, AMC, American Heroes Channel, Animal Planet, AXS TV, BBC America, beIN Sports, Bravo, Boomerang). New standalone scraper (scraper_timstreams.py) resolves each channel's embed page via a real headless browser to a direct, playable stream link, merged into the existing USA Live TV list alongside whatever DaddyLive's own channel scraper already provides (not a replacement, both are unioned together). v2.3.343 - Replaced TotalSportek entirely: the old totalsportek24.is live in-addon scrape (sports_sources.py) was confirmed unreliable, its per-sport pages frequently serving a generic all-sports-today page instead of anything scoped to the requested sport. The site's real current home is totalsportek.press, which needs Playwright to resolve its embed.st-based streams (same resolver DaddyLive already uses), so this is now a standalone scraper (scraper_totalsportek.py, same coordinator/per-sport-worker-process design as the DaddyLive rewrite this week) producing totalsportek.json, merged in via json_data.py. Confirmed live against a real match (Liverpool vs Leeds United): of the 40+ sources that page lists, only about 3 ever have a real, resolvable link at all (the rest are bare placeholder entries with nothing behind them) - this now correctly surfaces just those working ones instead of a pile of dead listings. v2.3.342 - Fixed 2 real sports date/time bugs. (1) The custom-skin sports events list (Home's Sports nav â€” a separate rendering path from the native events page) was displaying the raw scraped date/time string as-is: for most sources that's a UTC-labeled string baked in at scrape time with no conversion, for others it was genuinely blank. Now converts the event's start_ts through the device's own local timezone the same way the native page already did, with an honest "TBD" when no source had a parseable time at all. (2) StreamsEast (an actively-merged source for every sport) never actually captured any date/time from the site despite it being right there in the HTML â€” confirmed live each event card carries a real data-ts unix timestamp attribute that the scraper's regex just never looked for; now extracted and populated for every StreamsEast event. (MethStreams and TotalSportek24's primary scrape paths were already computing a correct start_ts internally â€” they just weren't being displayed correctly before fix #1.) v2.3.341 - Fixed unaired TV episodes still showing as playable in Favorites, the Home TV carousel, the Anticipated widget, and the TV Shows browse list. v2.3.338 fixed this for the native episode-list page (metadata_router.py's tv_season_episodes) and Continue Watching, but confirmed live that the custom-skin episode list used by all of the above (home.py's _open_tv_episodes) is a completely separate code path that calls meta.get_episodes() directly â€” it never picked up that air-date filter at all. Same fix applied here: an episode only counts as available once its air_date has actually passed. v2.3.340 - Fixed a real bug in the magnet library's episode filter: a season-pack release with no episode number in its name at all (e.g. "Lioness 2023 S02 1080p x265-ELiTE") was only checked for a full SxxExx marker, so with none found it fell through to "assume it matches any episode" â€” meaning a Season 2 pack could get treated as valid for a Season 3 Episode 1 request and get played instead of the real S03E01 file. Bare season numbers/ranges in a release name (no episode part) are now recognized as identifying their own season(s) and rejected unless the requested season is among them; only a release with no season indication at all (a plain "COMPLETE" bundle) still falls through to the old assume-it-matches default. Also fixed EZTV's cumulative magnet scraper only ever fetching page 1 of its API (missing older seasons past the first ~100 torrents for long-running shows) and cutting off 4K releases behind a too-low match cap â€” both raised/paginated properly, confirmed live against Game of Thrones' full 8-season catalogue. v2.3.339 - Dropped 2 sports sources confirmed to never actually deliver a playable stream despite successfully "finding" one: CrackStreams (its current player mechanism pushes video through an opaque blob: URL with no plain, network-sniffable .m3u8 request at all â€” a real run of its scraper produced zero events across every category) and RoxieStreams (its m3u8 CDN sits behind genuine Cloudflare bot-protection that blocks every non-browser client, confirmed to also fail in real Kodi playback). Both were found but never played â€” dropped rather than left as dead weight in the source list. v2.3.338 - Fixed 3 real, confirmed bugs where unaired TV episodes were treated as already available: (1) the season episode list showed every episode TMDB has an entry for, including ones with a blank or future air_date â€” a season with 8 announced episodes but only 1 actually aired showed all 8 as playable directory items; (2) Continue Watching surfaced a show as an "upcoming" card (with a release-date plot) the moment you finished the latest-aired episode, instead of just leaving it out of the row entirely until the real next episode airs; (3) the auto-play-next-episode feature (when enabled) would try to advance straight into that same not-yet-aired episode after finishing the current one. All three now use the same rule: an episode only counts as available once its air_date has actually passed. v2.3.337 - Wired in RoxieStreams as a new live sports source (json_data.py) â€” a free aggregator covering soccer/MLB/NBA/NFL/NHL/UFC/boxing/motorsports, scraped standalone (server-rendered HTML, no JS needed at all for this one, unlike every other sports source in this addon). v2.3.336 - Fixed sport icons not visibly updating after the v2.3.334 icon refresh for anyone who'd already browsed that sport before updating: Kodi caches every rendered image (Textures13.db) keyed by its exact file path, local files included, and does NOT compare file content/mtime â€” so overwriting an icon's PNG bytes at the unchanged path is invisible to Kodi for any icon already rendered once. Every sport icon file now carries a version suffix in its filename (soccer_v2.png, etc.) instead of a bare name, so Kodi is guaranteed to treat it as a brand-new file it's never cached before. This is now the permanent mechanism going forward â€” a future icon refresh just needs the version bump in sports_sources.py's _ICON_SET_VERSION, no manual cache-clear step ever required again. v2.3.335 - Fixed a real, confirmed bug in the cumulative magnet-library lookup (magnet_library.py): a TV show's library entry accumulates EVERY episode/season-pack ever found for it in one flat list (e.g. a real show had S02E03/E04/E06/E07/E08, a full S02 pack, and even a later season's S03E01 all mixed together) â€” get_cached_magnets() returned the whole pile for every request regardless of which specific episode was actually asked for, so a wrong-episode magnet could easily end up in the picker instead of (or ranked above) the real one. Now filters by season/episode the same way torrent_sources.py's own live-search filter already does (a release with no single-episode marker, like a season pack, is kept since it could legitimately contain the target episode; one that does name a specific episode must match exactly). Applies uniformly regardless of which scraper populated the entry â€” weekly EZTV, daily airing-today, or the newly-added personal TMDB-list source. Fixed by moving the BeautifulSoup import to inside the one function that uses it, so opening Sports (and everything that doesn't touch that specific scraper) no longer has any dependency on typing_extensions being present. v2.3.330 -Major overhaul of Movies/TV torrent search, root-caused live over an extended debugging session comparing against a real search that was both faster and more complete. Confirmed the previous architecture (pre-resolving every found torrent through RD/AD/PM/TB before ever showing the picker) was the actual cause of a persistent ~100s delay: with up to 10 candidates and only 5 workers, at least one was virtually always genuinely uncached, and the batch waited close to its own ceiling nearly every search, even when personal/free/embed sources had already settled in under 2 seconds. Root cause was a Python footgun â€” debrid_torrent.py wrapped the candidate-resolve batch in "with ThreadPoolExecutor(...) as pool:", and exiting a "with" block on an executor ALWAYS blocks until every submitted task finishes, no matter what timeout the results-collection loop itself uses. Fixed by managing the executor's shutdown manually (shutdown(wait=False)) instead of via "with", so the function returns as soon as collection is done rather than waiting on abandoned background threads. v2.3.327 - Fixed a real, user-confirmed false-negative in the shared title-match filter (used by every torrent source, so this benefits Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/Premiumize/TorBox alike, not just one service): searching a TV episode sends e.g. "Invasion S01E01" as the query, but the correct torrent is legitimately named "Invasion 2021 S01E01 Last Day..." â€” the release year sitting between the show name and the episode marker isn't a skip-word, so the contiguous-phrase match failed and a torrent the user had personally found on Knaben, confirmed correct, and added to their own AllDebrid was rejected as a "false match" by Starfleet's own search. Also fixed the actual cause of CFL games showing up mixed into the NFL listing itself (confirmed live: a real CFL game and a European League of Football game both appeared inside NFL) - the supplementary schedule source has no per-league split for American football, so it was merged in unfiltered for whichever of NFL/CFB/CFL happened to have a menu entry; now filtered by each game's real league name before merging, so NFL only shows NFL, CFL only shows CFL, etc. Both bugs together also explain why a real CFL game's own stream links weren't found when played from the (wrong) NFL section - the wrong sport was being passed to every stream resolver, none of which know to check CFL's actual listings when told to look for NFL. Fixed a narrow but real race condition behind the home screen occasionally failing to load a section on the first click (confirmed live, matched reports it "works on retry"): a background thread that pushes freshly-loaded data into the home screen can land mid-navigation and throw against an already-closing window; tightened from both sides so the window signals it's closing before doing anything else, and the background thread re-checks immediately before touching it. Also fixed the Sports section's page title showing a broken/unreadable placeholder character in the breadcrumb (e.g. "Videos / Starfleet / [?] Boxing") - a stadium/hockey emoji in the category title that this Kodi build's skin font can't render; replaced with plain text. Adult section: film titles are now cleaned of common scraping junk (duplicate year tags, resolution/release tags) before being displayed or used to check for a stream source - a mismatched messy title on one side of that check could cause a real, working film to be wrongly dropped as "no source"; the New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers listings were also found to skip the has-a-source check entirely (unlike every other Adult listing), so titles with no actual stream anywhere were shown and dead-ended on click - now filtered the same as everywhere else. Performer/actor search in the Adult section's unified search was a stub that always returned nothing ("no actor search API - skip for now") - built a real one backed by a cached full name index from the site's own per-letter actor pages. New sports stream source added (livetv902.me / livetv.sx family): covers a wide range of sports and leagues this addon didn't have a source for before; found via live investigation that its "alieztv"-type mirrors resolve through a plain, unobfuscated JS call to a real HLS URL - no WASM/P2P wall like embed.st - verified against a real live CFL game. Note: this source's availability was inconsistent in testing (worked reliably in some passes, not in others, without a clear cause) - it's wired in as a supplementary source alongside everything else, so it simply contributes nothing extra when it's not available rather than causing any problem. v2.3.219 - Fixed MLB Network and NHL Network (24/7 channels) not playing: verified live that daddylive.mov's signing CDN (fiveo4.casadenoval.uk) started rejecting every request with a bare 403, even a freshly-decoded, correctly-signed, not-yet-expired URL with the right Referer - this looked at first like the same un-fixable TLS-fingerprint wall documented elsewhere in this changelog for Cloudflare Turnstile, but confirmed by direct testing it isn't: the CDN now also requires the Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site "fetch metadata" headers a real browser always sends and that neither our scraper nor, importantly, Kodi's own player ever did - simply adding them (both to our own verification check and onto the URL Kodi's player actually opens, via the same header pipe-syntax already used elsewhere for Referer/User-Agent) resolves it. Also added a live-verification step this resolver was missing entirely: previously, once a mirror's obfuscated blob decoded into something that merely looked like a URL, that URL was handed straight to Kodi's player with no check that it would actually serve - now it's fetched and confirmed to return a real #EXTM3U playlist first, so a mirror that decodes but 403s (this exact bug) or serves an expired/dead link gets correctly skipped in favor of the next mirror instead of crashing playback. v2.3.218 - Fixed Adult section kicking the user all the way out of the addon on click, same class of bug as the Sports crash-out fixed in v2.3.216/217, but guaranteed to happen every time instead of intermittently: entering the Adult section shows a PIN entry prompt if one is set, and that prompt was popping up in the middle of the same window-activation sequence a Sports click goes through - any blocking dialog shown at that exact moment can make Kodi abandon the transition. The PIN check now happens before the home screen even starts navigating away, not during it. Also fixed a related bug found while fixing this: the "only ask for the PIN once per session" behavior never actually worked, because this addon runs with reuselanguageinvoker off (a fresh Python process per call, confirmed in addon.xml) - the old code stored the unlock flag in a plain in-memory variable that reset on every single click, silently re-prompting for the PIN every time despite the setting's own description promising otherwise. Now persisted properly so it actually only asks once. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is noticeably larger now - the previous release's ~2% bump turned out to be too subtle to see; also enlarged the matching per-row focus borders (there were two overlapping highlight mechanisms in the skin, only one of which was resized last time). v2.3.217 - Follow-up to v2.3.216's navigation fix, based on further live testing on the Firestick: the previous release stopped the "kicked all the way out of the addon" symptom, but a deeper live test showed the fix's own two-step handoff (jump to an empty placeholder screen first, then swap in the real category a moment later) could still get stuck - the second step silently failing to fire, leaving the user stranded on a permanently empty screen instead of the Sports (or Movies/TV/Live TV/Adult) page they clicked. Replaced that two-step handoff with a single direct jump straight to the clicked category, removing the fragile middle step entirely. Trade-off: Back out of a category may now return to Kodi's previous screen instead of this addon's home screen in some cases, rather than a category that may not load at all - confirmed working live against Sports. v2.3.216 - Fixed a real crash-on-navigate bug found by live-testing on the Firestick: clicking Sports (or any top-nav category) in the home screen could silently kick the user all the way out of the addon back to Kodi's own Add-ons screen, with no error dialog. Also: the dependency-check prompt (offers to install ResolveURL) was re-running on every single in-app navigation click, not just on first launch - could pop a blocking install prompt mid-navigation for no reason connected to what was actually clicked; now only runs when Home is genuinely (re)launching. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is now slightly larger (~2%) per user request, for better visibility. v2.3.215 - Fixed three real skin-navigation bugs found by live-testing on the Firestick with ADB: (1) an unprompted auto-relaunch, where backing all the way out to Kodi's own Add-ons screen would spontaneously reopen Starfleet's home a moment later with zero input - root cause was the addon's own root action relaunching Home on ANY visit to its plugin:// root with no fresh lock file present, including background metadata queries from Kodi/the active Kodi skin (e.g. Add-ons tile widgets), not just genuine user launches; now only relaunches when the Videos window is actually the one on screen. (2) The home screen's hero banner (title/plot/Play/More Info) could get stuck showing a previous section's item when switching to a section with no content yet (e.g. Live TV with no favorites saved) - it's now cleared instead of left stale. (3) Moving left/right at the very edge of a carousel row could unexpectedly jump focus to the top nav bar instead of stopping at the row - the row lists were missing their own left/right wrap targets, letting Kodi's automatic proximity navigation take over.\nv2.3.214 - Added a new working stream resolver: streame.center, a shared embed backend used by several front-end sites (e.g. powerstreams.site, realsportshd.buzz) that a raw embed link alone can't play (its ch##.php/hls.php pages need a decrypt.php exchange first, done automatically now) - verified live against a real MLB game. Rather than write one scraper per front-end site (most of them have no real schedule of their own to scrape - one 403s outright, another is just a static link directory), this runs as a universal post-processing step across every existing source (StreamsEast, CrackStreams, etc), so any sport those sources already cover gets this fix automatically the moment one of them happens to route through streame.center. Also fixed the repo's own landing page (index.html) linking to a stale repository.starfleet-1.0.11.zip instead of the current 1.0.13 - a fresh install via that page was pulling the old repository add-on even though addons.xml itself was already correct.\nv2.3.213 - Fixed CrackStreams returning 0 events for every sport, every time: its event-listing page was being fetched at /league/mlbstreams (etc.), which is a 404 - the site moved to /category/mlb/ (etc.) a while back, and even that correct page no longer has any scrapable per-game links in its static HTML (JS-rendered listing, like most of this ecosystem now). Rather than reverse-engineer another discovery API, this now builds the event page URL directly from the two team names in the title (CrackStreams' own URL pattern is the predictable /stream/<team>-vs-<team>, tried in both team orders) - verified live against a real game that this correctly finds the page and extracts its actual stream list, where before it always found nothing. Note: depending on the specific event, CrackStreams' own links may route through the same embed.st-family WASM-gated hosts documented as unfixable in previous releases - that's a limitation of whichever embed provider that event happens to use, not of this fix.\nv2.3.212 - New working stream source for MLB/NBA/NHL/NFL: mlb24all.ir and its sibling sites (nba24all.ir, nhl24all.ir, nfl24all.ir) were already listed in this addon's own code as a planned source, but the implementation was dead - it scraped for HTML anchor links that stopped existing once those sites became client-rendered apps, and it was never actually wired into the stream picker to begin with. Replaced it with a real implementation found via live network inspection: these sites run a clean, unauthenticated JSON API (GET .../api/v3/stateshot for the game/team catalogue, POST .../api/v2/generate_stream_info for a direct playable HLS link) - no login, no obfuscation, no WASM, just a straightforward API call. Verified live against an in-progress Blue Jays vs Rays game: returns real, independently-confirmed-working ESPN Home/Away broadcast links. This runs alongside every other source in the same merged link dialog, so a game covered by this source now shows up as extra "Link N" options next to StreamsEast/DaddyLive/etc.\nv2.3.211 - Fixed a real crash-on-play bug found by testing the Blue Jays game live on-device: the DaddyLive/TVNow24/7-channel resolver (used for the MLB/NHL Network channels and as the supplementary source merged into every sport event's link dialog) would, when none of a channel's mirrors could be decoded, hand back the raw unresolved mirror page URL on the theory that ResolveURL "might know it" â€” instead Kodi got a plain HTML page and crashed immediately with "error probing input format". Now returns nothing for that channel instead, so it's correctly dropped from the dialog rather than offered as a guaranteed-broken option. Also discovered and wired up a much more reliable resolution path for one whole class of these mirrors: some daddylive.mov mirrors point at tvnow247.top's own /embed/<channel> page, which used to fail outright (it's a client-rendered app with nothing scrapable in its HTML) â€” found via live network inspection that its player calls a clean JSON API (chat.cfbu247.sbs/api/resolve-dlstream) to get its real stream, so that's tried first now, with a live-playlist check before accepting it (a couple of channels' upstreams turned out to be genuinely offline right now, verified directly â€” not a scraper bug, just those specific feeds being down). StreamsEast (embed.st) links are confirmed to depend on a WASM+P2P ticket-exchange system with no static stream URL anywhere in the page - verified via live browser inspection that even a real browser only gets a playable stream after running embed.st's own obfuscated code, which can't be replicated from a Kodi Python addon - left as-is this release since that's a limitation of that specific host, not something scraping can fix.\nv2.3.210 - Fixed MLB (and every sport's) StreamsEast source: streamseast.is is dead (the domain no longer resolves at all); the site moved to streameasti.is with a different URL structure (no numeric event id, irregular section-name pluralization) and a different embed mechanism (source buttons carry a base64-encoded URL in a data-s attribute, swapped into the player by a JS click handler â€” the iframe's own src is always blank in the raw HTML, so the old scraper found nothing). Updated the domain, URL patterns, and added the data-s extraction, so StreamsEast now contributes real "Link N" options again for every sport, not just MLB. Verified against a real live Blue Jays game: get_event_streams now returns 3 StreamsEast links + 3 more from the TVNow247/DaddyLive source added in v2.3.209, all 6 shown together in one sequentially-numbered dialog (this merging was already automatic â€” fixing the two sources was the actual work). v2.3.209 - New: MLB Network 24/7 channel added to the MLB section â€” selecting it shows a Link 1/2/3 picker across three known-good daddylive.mov mirrors. New: full Live TV source added â€” TVNow247 (500+ channels scraped from tvnow247.top, adult channels excluded). New: live sports events scraped from tvnow247.top/schedule.json are now merged into each sport's event listing and used as a supplementary stream source everywhere, categorized by sport automatically. Fixed a real bug found while building these: the daddylive.mov channel resolver assumed every mirror-list JSON entry has the same {name,url} shape, but some pages use {name,id,url} with an extra field in between â€” entries in that shape were silently never matching. Also fixed: numeric-only channel ids (this addon's own MLB "399" test case, plus most of TVNow247's catalogue) were falling back to parsing the page's title tag for the real channel name, but title formats vary wildly ("Free X Live...", "Watch X Online...", "X Live Stream Free...") and that guess was unreliable â€” callers that already know the real name (the new TV channel list, the new events scraper) now pass it through explicitly instead of guessing, which took random-sample channel resolution from 0% to 100% in testing. v2.3.208 - v2.3.207 verified live: NHL Network now resolves and plays (confirmed reaching video decode), and Back from Movies/TV Shows/etc now correctly returns to the home screen. This release fixes the one remaining piece: the carousel focus highlight still wasn't showing, because the id=90 overlay control had a hardcoded <visible>false</visible> in the skin XML â€” Kodi re-evaluates XML visible conditions continuously, which silently overrides/no-ops any Python setVisible(True) call. Removed the XML condition; visibility is now owned entirely by home.py (explicitly hidden on init, shown/positioned on focus). v2.3.207 - NHL Network 24/7 channel still didn't play after v2.3.205's onhockey.tv fix, because onhockey.tv's own proxy for that channel (daddylive.php) is dead (404). Now resolves directly via daddylive.mov's channel mirror list, decoding the obfuscated embed script one mirror tier uses to get a fresh signed .m3u8. Also: fixed Adult section movie posters occasionally showing a neighboring film's cover art (nearest-match bug in the cover-art scraper). Also: home screen carousel focus highlight (the orange selection border on Movies/TV/etc rows) now actually renders â€” it was never appearing on some devices/Kodi builds even though selection itself worked. Also: Back from a section (Movies/TV Shows/etc) now correctly returns to the home screen instead of exiting past the addon into Kodi's own Videos section. v2.3.206 - Fix free/non-debrid streams not resolving: script.module.resolveurl was marked optional and pinned to a stale version (5.1.28) that was never actually hosted anywhere, so it was silently never installed. Now required, bumped to the real published 5.1.206, and pulled from the repository's new smrzips repo dir. v2.3.205 - Fix NHL Network (Sports section) not playing: onhockey.tv's live-channel page (used for the 24/7 NHL Network stream) embeds its player via JS config (src/file/source: "...m3u8") or a same-domain proxy iframe, not the plain stream links the scraper was looking for. Added JS-embedded m3u8 detection and a same-domain iframe follow-through, matching the extraction already used successfully for this exact channel in the Live TV section.

extension.description: Elementum is a torrent finding and streaming engine. It doesn't go on torrent websites for legal reasons. However, it calls specially crafted add-ons (called providers) that are installed separately. This project is a fork of the well known, but no longer maintained Pulsar/Quasar projects from steeve and scakemyer. NOTE: install plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.zip from the repository first, then manually install the matching plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.<platform>.zip on top for your device's platform (e.g. windows_x64, android_arm64, linux_x64) and restart Kodi - binaries are split into per-platform zips to stay under GitHub's 100MB file size limit.
extension.disclaimer: The author does not own or host any content found within this Addon. The author is not connected to or in any other way affiliated with Kodi, Team Kodi, or the XBMC Foundation.

extension.description: GitHub-backed repository for the Elementum torrent addon.

extension.description: Elementum Burst is a lean and mean multi-provider for Elementum.
