extension.description: Resolves video player and host addresses to playable streams. Covers sports, live and adult hosts that other resolvers do not, and falls back to ResolveURL for every host it knows.
extension.news: v1.4.12 - The Byse family also answers to mfw09.org. v1.4.11 - Host updates: Facebook (reels and share links), Filemoon, LBRY / Odysee, OK.ru, PeerTube, Streamix, StreamRuby, Vidzy and VOE follow the changes their sites made, and three new hosts are supported (Content.st, StreamOrigin, UFOload). The Byse / Filemoon family now matches any of its domains (new ones such as byseraguci no longer fail with "no resolver") and gets longer to solve its puzzle, so fewer links give up when the puzzle is a hard one. A host that just timed out is skipped for a few minutes instead of being waited on again by the second resolver and the page walk (a dead host now fails in about 15 s instead of 50 s). Checked against 73 live links from 42 hosts: 63 resolve, against 33 for the stock resolver on the same links. v1.4.10 - Maintenance release: every player family was checked again against live pages (YouTube and short links, Vimeo, Archive.org, Dailymotion, Rutube, VixSrc, Global News, RockyLive, embed.st, the Ripple/Kora channels, CDN Live and the DLHD channels) and resolves to a playlist or file that really answers; the YouTube notes were brought up to date. v1.4.9 - File-host links (Nitroflare, Rapidgator, 1fichier and others) whose address ends in a file name such as .mkv or .mp4 are no longer mistaken for a playable stream; they go to your debrid service. v1.4.8 - CDN Live players: cdnlivetv.tv / cdnlivetv.is channel player pages (the signed playlist is built in the page from encoded pieces) now resolve, so the live sports channels and the channels listed against each fixture play. v1.4.7 - TimStreams players: the ehgembxe.cfd / epiembeds.online / embeds.gay player frames (signed playlist fetched through a token address and unscrambled) now resolve, so TimStreams live events and its 24/7 channels play; also read by the generic page reader. v1.4.6 - New resolver: Global News live (globalnews.ca/live/ national plus the regional newscasts - Toronto, Calgary, Edmonton, BC, Montreal, Halifax, Winnipeg and more), free and without DRM; checked on 7 of 7 regions tested. v1.4.5 - DASH (.mpd) streams, live TV included: player pages that name a manifest now resolve to it together with the details a protected stream needs (ClearKey key pairs or a Widevine licence address, passed on in the same header tail), direct .mpd addresses pass through as before, and a manifest check is available to callers. v1.4.4 - New resolver: Vidrift embeds (movie and TV pages by TMDB id; original-audio stream first, full-HD HLS or MP4; checked end to end). v1.4.3 - internal test build, replaced by v1.4.4. v1.4.2 - Self-check on launch: when Kodi starts (and whenever the Starfleet plugin or ResolveURL settings change, and at most every 6 hours on first use) the resolver tests each debrid account it holds. If one went stale because ResolveURL or the plugin was paired again, the current working account is taken over after it passes the service's own check; a candidate that does not work is never kept and the account held before is put back. Nothing is written to the other add-on, switched-off services stay off. New "Check accounts now" button in the resolver settings. v1.4.1 -Faster and safer next to ResolveURL. Speed: the finished stream address is no longer requested a second time to test it (saves 0.3 to 0.65 s on every host that goes through the ResolveURL code, and stops valid streams being rejected: 33 of 41 test host families now play, 18 for the installed ResolveURL), MixDrop resolves natively first, prefetch(urls) plus a 90-second on-disk memory let a link that was resolved in the background open instantly. No conflicts with ResolveURL: the copied code no longer installs a process-wide URL opener or switches Python to unverified HTTPS, and the pairing script moved off the import path. Debrid accounts imported from ResolveURL or the plugin are read-only (nothing is written to the other add-on), re-read when a token goes stale, and an item that was already in your Debrid-Link seedbox or Offcloud account is never removed. v1.4.0 - New resolvers: YouTube (adaptive HLS up to 2160p from the iOS player, muxed fallback, YouTube add-on as last resort), X / Twitter (highest-bitrate MP4), Facebook (HD file from the embed player), TikTok (highest bitrate; needs the page to load without TikTok bot check), VixSrc and Vidbolt movie and TV pages (TMDB addresses, full-HD playlists in under a second). A host that does not answer is skipped for 90 seconds so one dead site never costs several time-outs; connections give up after 6 seconds. DLHD mirrors dlhd.pk, dlhd.st and dlhd.net added; Gofile uses the current website-token scheme. Re-checked all 269 hosts on the dead list: none came back. v1.3.0 - Live sports pages: the generic page reader now hands any player host Starfleet knows to its own resolver (so a game page that only embeds a known player resolves end to end), direct playlist or media addresses pass straight through, and it understands more embed formats (layered-XOR payloads, worker pages, plain source variables, 16-bit byte arrays) plus the gsports.lat player. v1.2.0 - Mega-Debrid can now be paired (login and password, asked for once, checked before it is kept; the Starfleet plugin and ResolveURL logins are imported automatically), and its 140 live hosters are used for routing. Services that accept any link (TorBox, which takes every site yt-dlp supports) are tried as a last resort for addresses no host list names. v1.1.2 - Filemoon and the other Byse-based hosts (proof-of-work puzzle, 5 to 25 seconds) now get a longer time budget, so they resolve reliably instead of timing out at 14 seconds (9 of 9 test runs now play, was 4 of 9). v1.1.1 - New native resolvers for hosts that failed in a live test: Dailymotion, Archive.org, Rutube, PeerTube, Vimeo, Streamable, YouJizz, RedTube, XNXX/XVideos (each checked on current videos except XNXX). A list of 243 host names that no longer exist is built in, so links to them fail at once instead of waiting. v1.1.0 - Starfleet now carries its own copy of all the ResolveURL host resolvers (217 resolvers, 1007 domains) plus the adult extension resolvers (79 more), so every host ResolveURL knows is resolved by Starfleet first; the installed ResolveURL add-on stays as the last-chance fallback in case it was updated before this copy. Debrid-Link and Offcloud can now download a torrent that is not cached yet. v1.0.1 - free direct resolvers for MediaFire, Gofile, Pixeldrain, Dropbox, Google Drive, Sendspace, Solidfiles, Upload.ee, Files.fm and XFileSharing-style hosts (Vidoza, ClipWatching, GoUnlimited, Vidlox, VidUP, VUP, Uppit, Up-load, Uploadrar, TusFiles, DDownload, Racaty and more), plus Mp4upload, YourUpload and Sendvid as a second chance. Verified on real links: MediaFire, Pixeldrain, Upload.ee, Files.fm, Dropbox, Google Drive, Mp4upload, YourUpload, Sendvid. Hosts that no longer exist (GoUnlimited, Mystream, Vidlox, Fembed, VUP, UpVID, Racaty and others) now fail at once instead of waiting on fallbacks. v1.0.0 - first release: embed.st and embedsports players, embedsports.me, streame.center, shared gooz player, rockylive, vidload, gbsagbo, site-hosted video; MixDrop, DoodStream and StreamTape as a second chance after ResolveURL.

extension.summary: Starfleet video host resolver - pair debrid accounts, test a link
extension.description: Front door of the Starfleet Resolver (script.module.starfleetresolve), the resolver other add-ons can use to turn host and player addresses into playable streams. Pair Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox, Debrid-Link and Offcloud, import accounts from the Starfleet plugin or ResolveURL, see what is paired, and test any link. Installing this add-on installs the resolver module with it.
extension.news: v1.0.3 - requires resolver 1.4.7 (TimStreams players, self-check of paired accounts, DASH streams), so updating this add-on updates the resolver too. v1.0.2 - requires resolver 1.3.0. v1.0.1 - Mega-Debrid can be paired from this menu. v1.0.0 - first release: a visible Program add-on for the Starfleet Resolver module, so it can be found and installed on its own from the Starfleet repository.

extension.description: The scraping half of Starfleet: movie, TV, torrent, sports, live TV, radio and adult scrapers that the Starfleet add-on (and any add-on that wants them) calls. Menus, metadata and widgets stay in the add-on that uses it. Updated on its own, so a broken site can be fixed without updating the whole add-on. Can also be chosen as the external scraper module of add-ons that load one, and can run other installed scraper modules for Starfleet.
extension.news: v1.3.16 - Live TV and adult channels checked one by one: the DLHD 24/7 list, its Big Brother section and the tvnow247 list are left out while their sites cannot be reached (and come back by themselves), two dead news feeds (NASA TV, ABC News Live) are removed, and the adult TV list keeps only the channels whose playlist really answers (three dead ones dropped). v1.3.15 - A search made ahead of time for something not on screen (the next episode, today's new episode) asks only the torrent sources that are switched on (the best three in the automatic mode, no extras) and the debrid service: no release sites, no Usenet. v1.3.14 - The scrapers detect the device they run on (a Fire TV Stick, an NVIDIA SHIELD, a PC...) and size themselves to it: a weak device runs fewer searches at once and keeps fewer results per source (about 40 % fewer threads and a third less memory when every source is on), a strong one keeps everything; the choice can be forced in Settings (Device). The title filter for add-ons that load this module is run once over the whole list instead of once per release. The source list no longer waits for your Requests library (the cloud-folder scan took 15-35 s every 15 minutes): the last list is used at once while a fresh one is built in the background, and it is built once after Kodi starts. v1.3.13 - Much faster movie / TV / anime torrent search: the best three sources (movies: Comet, StremThru, DMM; TV: Comet, Bitmagnet, TorrentDownloads; anime: Comet plus the anime sites) go first and the picker usually opens in 1-2 s instead of 5-7 s; the other sources start only when those find little, so rare titles still get the whole sweep (setting: Torrent sources > Automatic / My own choice). Releases with a Chinese or Russian title in front or a site tag ("47BT", "www.site.com") are no longer thrown away - that was most of the 4K releases other scraper modules found and this one did not - and DVD rips / 480p releases stay in the list, last (setting). Add-ons that load this module as their scraper module get the same six best sources on by default (1.7 s instead of 4-15 s for a film) and a time limit per source. A source that keeps coming back empty or late is left out for 24 hours (48 on a repeat) and tried again by itself. Stream rows show HDR / Dolby Vision / Atmos / REMUX and mark upscaled "4K" releases, which are listed last. v1.3.12 - The Cloudflare helper the scrapers use now ships inside this module (it was bundled in the Starfleet add-on), so every site that needs it also works when this module runs under another add-on. v1.3.11 - Declared the same way as other scraper modules (start-up service entry, icon and fanart) so it is listed in the repository browser. v1.3.10 - Starfleet Scrapers now shows in the repository browser and the Program add-ons list like other scraper modules, and opens its settings when started. v1.3.9 -Faster searches. Movie / TV torrent search starts the quick aggregators first and only starts the single-site scrapers if those have not produced enough hits within about a second, so the picker opens in roughly 1-3 s instead of 5-7 s (titles with few hits still ask every source). Free streaming sites: the dead-link check waits at most 2.5 s, remembers what it found, and a title searched again within five minutes comes back instantly. v1.3.8 - Listed as an executable add-on so it can be found in the repository browser. v1.3.7 - Works properly as the scraper module of other add-ons: the torrent results it hands over are now only the ones for the title asked for (no more sequels, other shows, multi-film collections or wrong episodes), carry the release tags that quality / HDR / codec labels are read from, show their size (also when the site gives it in bytes or only in the name) and use the 40-character hash that debrid cache checks need. Season packs and complete-series packs are offered too, for the sources that have them. v1.3.6 - Sports: every stream in the stream list now shows its quality (4K, 1080p, 720p, 480p, SD). It is read from the stream's own playlist, or estimated from its bitrate and marked with ~ when the playlist does not say; slower servers fill their label in a few seconds later. v1.3.5 - Sports: team matching and late / overtime game detection on the live scoreboards, used by the add-on's My Teams home row and alerts. v1.3.4 - Sports: the first game opened after Kodi starts on a Fire TV no longer ends with "no stream links / the event may not have started". The sources are slow while everything is cold, so the stream search now keeps waiting for the first links instead of giving up empty (up to 45 s), then closes a few seconds after the first one arrives. v1.3.3 - Sports: game times now show on Fire TV.
